trigger: The argv array is sized for i+3 slots - `newargs = (my_stupid_string *) apr_palloc(cont, sizeof (char *) * (i + 3));` at threadproc/unix/proc.c:325-326 of the vulnerable file (git show a26a90f27^:threadproc/unix/proc.c) - and holds SHELL_PATH, "-c" and i arguments, so the terminator belongs at newargs[i+2]. The code wrote `newargs[i + 3] = NULL;` (line 334 of that file): one pointer slot past the end, while newargs[i+2] was left uninitialised and passed to execve as part of argv.
poc: any APR_SHELLCMD apr_proc_create; the reported symptom was intermittent execve EFAULT
notes: Two defects on one pool object: an 8-byte OOB write of NULL past a pool-carved pointer array, and an uninitialised read of newargs[i+2] handed straight to execve. Both are invisible to a heap checker - the array is bump-carved out of a memnode, so slot i+3 is simply the next object, and apr_palloc does not zero (only apr_pcalloc does, memory/unix/apr_pools.c:917). The bug reached anyone only because execve validated the pointer and returned EFAULT; the write itself never faulted.

trigger: Pre-fix apr_pstrndup did `res = apr_palloc(a, n + 1); memcpy(res, s, n);` with no check that s actually holds n bytes. Every caller that passed a maximum length rather than an exact one over-read the source string by up to n - strlen(s) bytes.
poc: apr_pstrndup(p, short_string, large_n)
notes: The over-read source is whatever the caller passed; in APR/httpd that is overwhelmingly another pool string, so the read stays inside the same memnode and returns adjacent request data instead of faulting. Destination `apr_palloc(a, n + 1)` in the same function. Author's own note calls it theoretical - it is exactly the class the arena makes theoretical, because the read cannot be observed. Fix strlen's the source first and copies min(len, n).

trigger: `size = APR_ALIGN_DEFAULT(size)` in apr_palloc and `size = APR_ALIGN(size + APR_MEMNODE_T_SIZE, BOUNDARY_SIZE)` in allocator_alloc wrapped for sizes near SIZE_MAX, so a huge request returned a small block; the caller then wrote what it asked for.
poc: apr_palloc(p, n) with n within APR_ALIGN_DEFAULT's rounding distance of SIZE_MAX
fix_commit: 19cdf7c8c9e5a56e996961c2ec791254a8bb5687 (0.9.x r800733) plus b6b7d26cd / fe1450d79 / 27a039c7b on the other branches
notes: ALLOCATOR-INTERNAL - flagged because the survey deliberately excludes allocator bugs from the 'ordinary code' story. The defect is in the pool allocator itself, not in a consumer, and it also hit apr_rmm, APR's second region allocator over shared memory. Kept in the table only so the category is visible, and it should be counted separately from the consumer rows. It is still `blind` for the same structural reason as those: apr_palloc hands back a raw interior pointer into a memnode with no per-object bound, so the short block the wrap produced is indistinguishable from a correct one at the point of use. Fix adds post-alignment overflow checks (`if (size < in_size) return NULL;`) and drops the redundant alignment in apr_pcalloc.

trigger: `*newpath = apr_pmemdup(p, path, pathlen + 1);` at file_io/win32/filepath.c:952 copied pathlen+1 bytes out of a buffer that only holds pathlen valid ones, then re-terminated. One byte of adjacent, possibly uninitialised pool memory was read on every merge.
poc: any apr_filepath_merge on Windows; flagged by memory-checking tools
notes: `path` is the caller's pool buffer; apr_pmemdup allocates the destination with apr_palloc. The commit message is explicit that it was 'harmless other than triggering errors from tools that check memory access' - which is the survey's point in miniature: the only reason anyone knew is that a tool with a model of object extents complained, and neither malloc nor the pool has such a model for a bump-carved string. Fix uses apr_pstrmemdup, which copies exactly pathlen and terminates.

trigger: `static const int dayoffset[12]` is indexed by the caller-supplied xt->tm_mon with no range check, so an apr_time_exp_t whose tm_mon came from an untrusted date string reads outside the table.
poc: apr_time_exp_get() on an apr_time_exp_t with tm_mon outside 0..11 (e.g. from a parsed HTTP date)
notes: CONTROL-GROUP row, and the alloc_arena value is a bucketing compromise: the object read out of bounds is not heap at all but a file-scope `static const int dayoffset[12]` in .rodata (time/unix/time.c:142). Nothing in the enum covers statics; it is recorded as the non-arena bucket. A bounded-globals ABI (CHERI gives each global its own capability) catches this; a pool is not involved. Fix adds `if (xt->tm_mon < 0 || xt->tm_mon >= 12) return APR_EBADDATE;`.

trigger: Same dayoffset[12] out-of-range index as CVE-2017-12613. The 1.6.x fix (r1807976) was never merged to the 1.7.x branch, so APR 1.7.0 shipped the bug again and it was re-assigned.
poc: same as CVE-2017-12613
notes: CONTROL-GROUP row and a regression of CVE-2017-12613, recorded separately because it is a distinct advisory against a distinct version range (1.7.0 only). Same .rodata `static const int dayoffset[12]`; see the CVE-2017-12613 row for the alloc_arena caveat.

affected_function: apr_encode_base64 / apr_encode_base64_binary / apr_encode_base32* / apr_encode_base16, via apr_pencode_base64 & siblings (encoding/apr_encode.c)
trigger: The two-pass API sizes with dest==NULL then encodes. The sizing pass computed `*len = ((slen + 2) / 3 * 4) + 1` in signed apr_ssize_t (git show 622905ddf^:encoding/apr_encode.c lines 271 and 333) and never rejected a negative slen; the encode pass indexed with a plain `int i` (same pre-fix file, lines 288 and 297). A caller-controlled slen near SSIZE_MAX, or negative, wraps the size, apr_palloc returns a short pool buffer, and the encode loop writes 4/3*slen bytes into it.
poc: apr_pencode_base64(p, src, slen, 0, &len) with slen chosen so ((slen+2)/3*4)+1 wraps
notes: APR CHANGES text: 'Integer Overflow or Wraparound vulnerability in apr_encode functions ... allows an attacker to write beyond bounds of a buffer.' Destination: `encoding/apr_encode.c:346 char *cmd = apr_palloc(p, size);` in apr_pencode_base64 in the vulnerable tree (git show 622905ddf^:encoding/apr_encode.c; the same call is :357 in current trunk), with the identical shape in apr_pencode_base64_binary and the base32/base16 wrappers. Blind twice over: the object has no bounds of its own, and the memnode it sits in is 8 KB+ so a moderate overrun stays inside one malloc'd block. Fix moves the arithmetic to apr_size_t, rejects slen<0, and returns APR_ENOSPC when the source cannot be encoded.

trigger: The WSABUF count is accumulated into `apr_int32_t nvec` by a loop that adds one entry per APR_DWORD_MAX chunk of each iovec (lines 99-106 of the vulnerable file, git show 27046d793^:network_io/win32/sendrecv.c). With large enough iovecs nvec overflows int32; the following `pWsaBuf = (nvec <= WSABUF_ON_STACK) ? _alloca(sizeof(WSABUF) * (nvec)) : malloc(sizeof(WSABUF) * (nvec));` (line 108 of that file) then reserves too little, and the fill loop (lines 113-131) writes past it.
poc: apr_socket_sendv on Windows with iovecs totalling more than INT32_MAX*APR_DWORD_MAX
fix_commit: a783ca8b7 (Win32: stop apr_socket_sendv splitting iovecs across WSABUFs), 3bbe15b4b (1.8.x r1904715), 96b81a069 (1.7.x r1904716), 435c7fc0d (32-bit apr_size_t follow-up)
notes: CONTROL-GROUP row. APR CHANGES: 'On Windows, APR 1.7.0 and earlier may write beyond the end of a stack based buffer in apr_socket_sendv(). This is a result of integer overflow.' The buffer is a dynamic stack allocation via _alloca at line 108 of git show 27046d793^:network_io/win32/sendrecv.c (WSABUF_ON_STACK is 50, network_io/win32/sendrecv.c:37 in current trunk, where the fixed call at :109 sizes by in_vec instead), which CHERI bounds like any other stack object, so a per-object-bounds machine traps on the first out-of-range WSABUF store. Windows-only; nothing here touches an APR pool.

trigger: RFC6874 IPv6 zone-id re-encoding allocated `hostcopy = apr_palloc(p, len + 2);` at line 143 of the vulnerable file (git show 5d2ccf83a^:uri/apr_uri.c) but the writer emits len+2 content bytes and then terminates with `hostcopy[len + 2] = '\0';` at line 149 of that file - index len+2 in a len+2-byte object. One NUL byte past the pool allocation, for any link-local hostname containing a '%'. Current trunk carries the fixed `hostcopy = apr_palloc(p, len + 3);` at uri/apr_uri.c:163.
poc: apr_uri_parse + apr_uri_unparse on a URI such as http://[fe80::1%25eth0]/
fix_commit: 471de34e0f3f77af5d943df60b6c2e1ed9b8a5ea (trunk r1927941); the earlier 5d2ccf83a63656b11e4aae81980fafd3ae0e9955 (r1927940) moved the write instead and truncated the output
fixed_in: APR trunk / 2.0-dev only (introduced 8ddc303fd on 2025-08-21, never in a 1.x release)
notes: Live example of the arena hiding a real bug: found by APR's UBSan CI, not by ASAN, and the first attempted fix (r1927940) moved the NUL back inside the buffer and silently truncated the last data byte - a correctness regression that a bounds check would not have flagged either. The one-byte NUL lands on the next bump-allocated object in the same memnode and no allocator-level checker can see it. Fix enlarges the allocation to len+3 and restores the write at len+2. Trunk-only, so no released version is affected.

trigger: apr_sha1_base64 advanced its input past a leading `{SHA}` marker (`clear += APR_SHA1PW_IDLEN;` at crypto/apr_sha1.c:355) but left `len` at the ORIGINAL strlen, so apr_sha1_update hashed 5 bytes past the end of the plaintext. Triggered whenever the supplied plaintext password itself begins with `{SHA}`.
poc: HTTP Basic auth against a {SHA} htpasswd entry with the client-supplied password starting `{SHA}`
notes: Not a CVE - a PR-tracked buffer overrun, included because the arena story is exact. The over-read buffer is the caller's plaintext; on httpd's Basic-auth path that is `server/protocol.c:1715 t = ap_pbase64decode(r->pool, auth_line);` -> `server/util.c:2503 decoded = (char *) apr_palloc(p, apr_base64_decode_len(bufcoded));`, i.e. r->pool. Five bytes past a pool string are simply the next bump-allocated object, so the read succeeds silently and the hashed value depends on unrelated request data. The output buffer `char sample[120]` at crypto/apr_md5.c:701 is stack and is NOT the problem. Fix deletes the pointer advance.

trigger: On a failed multi-get, mget_conn_result called ms_bad_conn(ms, conn) - which destroys the connection and returns its slot to the apr_reslist - and then unconditionally called ms_release_conn(ms, conn) on the same connection, releasing it a second time. The server_queries hash entry was also deleted only at the end, so the iteration walked an entry that had already been handled.
poc: an apr_memcache_multgetp against a server that closes the connection mid-batch
notes: BORDERLINE. Commit title is 'Fix apr_memcache_multgetp memory corruption'. The doubly-released object is an apr_memcache_conn_t, `memcache/apr_memcache.c:415 conn = apr_palloc(np, sizeof( apr_memcache_conn_t ));` out of a per-connection sub-pool, and the release target is an apr_reslist, not the system allocator. Nothing reaches free(), so this produces aliasing - two callers holding the same live connection - rather than a libc double-free, and no heap checker has an event to fire on. That absence of a free event is precisely what makes pool/reslist lifetime bugs unreachable for allocator-level tooling. Fix splits the server-up and conn-up flags and moves the hash delete to the top.

affected_function: apr_strmatch_precompile (strmatch/apr_strmatch.c), plus the matching reads in match_boyer_moore_horspool*
trigger: The Boyer-Moore-Horspool skip table is indexed with a plain `char`: `shift[(int)s[i]] = ...` and `shift[apr_tolower(s[i])] = ...`. Any byte >= 0x80 in the pattern sign-extends to -128..-1, so the store lands at shift[-1]..shift[-128], i.e. 8 to 1024 bytes BEFORE the table.
poc: apr_strmatch_precompile(p, pattern, 1) with a pattern byte >= 0x80 (httpd reaches this from mod_substitute / mod_proxy_html pattern configuration and from Content-Type matching)
fix_commit: a7fc9eef25bad1d84d9f31a5051d8ac85b3ba0f2 (0.9.x r779994), 97e793b8b (apr side), backported from r779878
notes: One of the cleanest arena cases in the set. `strmatch/apr_strmatch.c:99 shift = (apr_size_t *)apr_palloc(p, sizeof(apr_size_t) * NUM_CHARS);` (NUM_CHARS=256, so 2 KB) is bump-allocated immediately after `pattern = apr_palloc(p, sizeof(*pattern));` at :90 in the SAME memnode. shift[-1] therefore overwrites the tail of the apr_strmatch_pattern_t that precedes it - including its `compare` function pointer - with an attacker-influenced length value. Both objects live inside one 8 KB memnode that APR obtained with a single malloc, so ASAN, a guard page, and a malloc-level checker all see a fully in-bounds store. Fix casts through unsigned char.

trigger: After apr_vformatter returned, the function unconditionally wrote `*(vd.vbuff.curpos) = '\0';`. When the formatted output exactly filled the buffer, curpos == buf + APR_BUCKET_BUFF_SIZE and the NUL landed one byte past the end of the stack array.
poc: any apr_brigade_printf whose formatted output is an exact multiple of APR_BUCKET_BUFF_SIZE
notes: CONTROL-GROUP row. Buffer: `buckets/apr_brigade.c:640 char buf[APR_BUCKET_BUFF_SIZE];` - a plain stack array, so a bounds-checking ABI catches the off-by-one immediately, and even a stack-protector build has a chance. Advisory framing is 'off-by-one overflow ... on big-endian platforms', where the clobbered byte was the significant end of an adjacent value and leaked. Fix deletes the write; the length is already tracked separately.

trigger: `nbytesdecoded = (((int)nprbytes + 3) / 4) * 3;` at lines 120 and 156 of the vulnerable apr-util file (git show 28136433^:encoding/apr_base64.c) casts an apr_size_t byte count to int. For an encoded input above ~1.4 GB the multiply overflows int, decode_len returns a small or negative size, the caller allocates that much, and apr_base64_decode then writes the full 3/4*n decode into the short buffer.
poc: apr_pbase64_decode / ap_pbase64decode on a base64 body larger than APR_BASE64_DECODE_MAX (2863311524)
notes: apr-util 1.x ships no pool wrapper of its own, so the destination is the caller's. The two real ones are both pools: APR trunk `encoding/apr_base64.c:211 decoded = (char *) apr_palloc(p, apr_base64_decode_len(bufcoded));` (apr_pbase64_decode) and httpd `server/util.c:2503 decoded = (char *) apr_palloc(p, apr_base64_decode_len(bufcoded));` (ap_pbase64decode, used by ap_get_basic_auth_pw at server/protocol.c:1715). Size and buffer come from the same overflowing expression, so the overflow is exactly as large as the wrap and lands entirely inside the request pool. Fix asserts the length limits and aborts.

trigger: Deeply nested XML from an untrusted source. start_handler built one apr_xml_elem per element with no depth cap, and apr_xml_quote_elem walks the resulting tree by direct recursion, one C frame per element, until the stack guard page is hit.
poc: apr-util's own regression input: test/data/nesting.xml, 2001 lines of nested elements, added by the fix commit
notes: BORDERLINE control-group row. The data structure being walked IS arena memory - `xml/apr_xml.c:157 elem = apr_pcalloc(parser->p, sizeof(*elem));` in the vulnerable 1.6.3 tree (git show 414e12e4^:xml/apr_xml.c; the same line is :143 in the current 1.7.x checkout) - but the memory that is actually exhausted is the call stack, one frame per level. CHERI bounds each stack allocation but does not bound recursion depth; what stops this is the guard page, which is independent of the allocator. Recorded as `stack`/`caught` on that reasoning. Fix caps depth at APR_XML_MAX_DEPTH=256 in start_handler.

trigger: A malicious or compromised Redis server answers a GET/INFO with a bulk-string header whose length is negative or <2. Pre-fix: `len = strtol(length, NULL, 10)` into an apr_size_t, so RESP's null bulk string `$-1\r\n` gives len=(apr_size_t)-1; `len != 0` so the else branch runs, apr_brigade_partition is called at len+2 == 1, apr_brigade_pflatten returns len==1, then `*new_length = len - 2` underflows to SIZE_MAX and `(*baton)[*new_length] = '\0'` writes at baton+SIZE_MAX, i.e. baton[-1] on a 64-bit wrap.
poc: Redis server reply `$-1\r\n` (or any bulk body that flattens to <2 bytes) to a GET issued by apr_redis_getp
notes: Affects apr-util 1.6.0-1.6.3. baton is allocated by apr_brigade_pflatten: `buckets/apr_brigade.c:294 *c = apr_palloc(pool, total);` (size = flattened brigade length). The bad write lands one byte BEFORE that pool object, i.e. on the tail of whatever apr_palloc bump-allocated just before it in the same memnode - no redzone, no header, no free() ever - so ASAN sees only the memnode's own malloc'd block and reports nothing. Second effect: *new_length = SIZE_MAX is returned to the caller as the value length, so httpd's mod_socache_redis / mod_session_redis then read SIZE_MAX bytes. Fix adds strtol errno/endptr validation, rejects val<0 and val>64MB, and guards len<2.

trigger: apr_memcache_stats parses a STATS reply. Each helper is invoked as `stat_read_X(p, conn->buffer + NAMELEN, conn->blen - NAMELEN)` (macros at :1711-1729) and then does `buf[len-2] = '\0'` to strip CRLF. A stat line whose remaining length is 0 or 1 makes len-2 wrap, and buf[SIZE_MAX]/buf[SIZE_MAX-1] resolves to buf[-1]/buf[-2] - a NUL written immediately before the pool buffer. When conn->blen < NAMELEN the offset is arbitrary.
poc: memcached STATS reply containing a matching stat keyword with no value and no CRLF, e.g. `STAT pid` truncated
notes: Same CVE as the version() site, different write site - recorded separately because the arena consequence differs (a write, not a read). Buffer: `memcache/apr_memcache.c:420 conn->buffer = apr_palloc(conn->p, BUFFER_SIZE + 1);`. Fix adds `if (len < 2) return ...;` to all four helpers plus the CRLF check in get_server_line.

trigger: A memcached server (or an attacker who can answer on its port) replies with a line beginning `VERSION` but shorter than MS_VERSION_LEN+2. Pre-fix: `apr_pstrmemdup(p, conn->buffer+MS_VERSION_LEN+1, conn->blen - MS_VERSION_LEN - 2)` - the apr_size_t subtraction underflows and apr_pstrmemdup memcpy's ~SIZE_MAX bytes out of the 513-byte connection buffer.
poc: memcached reply `VERSION\r\n` truncated so that conn->blen < 9
notes: Affects apr-util 1.3.0-1.6.3. Source buffer: `memcache/apr_memcache.c:420 conn->buffer = apr_palloc(conn->p, BUFFER_SIZE + 1);` with BUFFER_SIZE 512 (:22), out of the per-connection sub-pool created at :415. The over-read starts inside a pool memnode and walks off it; a bump allocator gives the buffer no upper bound of its own. Fix adds a `conn->blen < MS_VERSION_LEN + 2` guard plus CRLF validation in get_server_line (:678).

trigger: ASAN verdict 'Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1'. In the attribute scanner, a name terminated by ';' or ',' set `v = hde + 1` (pointing at the byte after the delimiter) and the loop tail then did `hdr = v + 1`, skipping TWO characters. For a Content-Type ending in ';' the delimiter is the last character, v is the NUL, and hdr becomes one byte past the allocation; `done` is not set for ';' so the do-while runs again and `switch (*hde)` reads that byte.
poc: Content-Type header value ending in a semicolon, e.g. 'multipart/form-data;'
notes: CONTROL-GROUP row as fuzzed; blind as deployed. Under the fuzzer the content_type string is `projects/apache-httpd/fuzz_preq.c:52 char *new_str2 = af_gb_get_null_terminated(&data2, &size2);` assigned at :64 `parser.content_type = new_str2;` -> `ada_fuzz_header.h:39 char *new_s = malloc(STR_SIZE + 1);`, a 76-byte malloc, so ASAN's redzone caught the +1 read. In httpd itself the same pointer is `modules/apreq/filter.c:144 const char *ct_header = apr_table_get(r->headers_in, "Content-Type");`, whose value string came from `server/protocol.c:348 *s = apr_palloc(p, current_alloc + 1);` on r->pool - bump-carved, so reading one byte past it just returns the next header in the same memnode. The fix sets v = hde (not hde+1) so hdr = v+1 lands exactly on the NUL, and separately rejects an absent/empty boundary before `ctx->bdry[blen] = 0` in create_multipart_context.

trigger: Send a request whose Connection: (or TE:, Upgrade:, Vary:) header value ends in token-stop characters, so ap_find_token's skip loop reaches the terminating NUL. The strict-parsing rewrite added in 2.2.32/2.4.24 marks NUL itself as T_HTTP_TOKEN_STOP, but the skip loop kept the old assumption that NUL is not a stop character and tested only TEST_CHAR(*s, T_HTTP_TOKEN_STOP) with no `*s &&` guard, so it walks past the end of the header value into adjacent pool bytes until it finds a byte that is a valid token character. Result is a segfault or a wrong token match (e.g. spurious keep-alive/close).
notes: Affected 2.4.24-2.4.25 and 2.2.32-2.2.33; introduced by the 2.2.32/2.4.24 HTTP strict-parsing change, per the advisory. Bug site read at b2445f6e1b^:server/util.c:1685 -- `while (TEST_CHAR(*s, T_HTTP_TOKEN_STOP)) { ++s; }` inside ap_find_token() at :1672, under a stale comment at :1682-1684 claiming 'NUL isn't a token stop, so we don't need to test for it'. That comment is false in this revision: b2445f6e1b^:server/gen_test_char.c:128 sets the flag with `if (!c || !(apr_isalnum(c) || strchr("!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~", c))) flags |= T_HTTP_TOKEN_STOP;` -- the leading `!c` makes NUL a stop character. Fix is `while (*s && TEST_CHAR(...))`. ALLOCATION SITE of the string walked off the end: the header value is not copied out of the line buffer, so `line` points into the request-header read buffer, read at b2445f6e1b^:server/protocol.c:297 -- `*s = apr_palloc(r->pool, current_alloc);` in ap_rgetline_core(), grown at :308 by `new_buffer = apr_palloc(r->pool, new_size);`. SIZE EXPRESSIONS: current_alloc = len (the first bucket's length); new_size = current_alloc * 2, or (bytes_handled + len) * 2 when that is larger. Caller path read at b2445f6e1b^:modules/http/http_protocol.c:273 `ap_find_token(r->pool, conn, "close")` and :276 `ap_find_token(r->pool, conn, "keep-alive")` with conn from apr_table_get(r->headers_in, "Connection"). The 2.2.x backport of the same fix is edb6db90d2474b5807b2459b3380bf947c5866fa (fixed in 2.2.34). fixed_in is 2.4.26: b2445f6e1b is contained in tag 2.4.26, though the CHANGES security entry only appears from tag 2.4.27. VERDICT blind: pool memnodes are packed with adjacent request objects and are reused without zeroing across apr_pool_clear, so the walk reads live neighbouring header data or stale bytes from a previous request with no bounds event.

trigger: A .htaccess file containing <Limit FOO> (or <LimitExcept>) naming a method not registered at config time; the disclosure is then read back by any later OPTIONS request via the Allow response header.
poc: https://github.com/hannob/optionsbleed
notes: OPTIONSBLEED, the archetype for this survey; every link below was read in the source by this session. (1) server/core.c:2471 ap_limit_section calls ap_method_register(cmd->pool, apr_pstrdup(cmd->pool, method)). In the .htaccess case cmd->pool == cmd->temp_pool, a REQUEST-SCOPED pool -- that identity is exactly what the fix tests: the patch adds 'if (cmd->pool == cmd->temp_pool) return apr_psprintf(...)' to refuse run-time registration. (2) The method-name string is apr_pstrdup'd from that request pool, i.e. bump-allocated at apr_pools.c:846-847 with no header and no owner. (3) register_one_method (modules/http/http_protocol.c:679-687) does apr_hash_set(methods_registry, methname, APR_HASH_KEY_STRING, pnum) at http_protocol.c:686, and methods_registry is a PROCESS-GLOBAL 'static apr_hash_t *' at http_protocol.c:676. (4) apr_hash_set STORES THE CALLER'S POINTER, it does not copy the key: 'he->key = key;' at apr/tables/apr_hash.c:316. So a global registry now holds a pointer into a request pool. (5) At end of request apr_pool_clear rewinds first_avail (apr_pools.c:968) and the bytes are handed out again UNZEROED to the next request. (6) A later OPTIONS request builds Allow via ap_make_method_list, walks the registry, and copies out whatever now occupies those recycled bytes -- another request's data. WHY CHERI IS BLIND: no free() ever occurs, so no revocation sweep can ever target this pointer; the capability in the hash table remains valid and IN BOUNDS because bounds were set on the whole ~8KB memnode at allocator_alloc's malloc (apr_pools.c:399), never on the pstrdup'd string. The pool does not scrub, so the stale bytes are live data rather than a trap representation. httpd's own CHANGES entry for 2.4.28 calls this 'Corrupted or freed memory access'. Affected 2.2.x and 2.4.0-2.4.27. || SUBAGENT-CORROBORATION: OPTIONSBLEED, the archetype for this survey. Chain, all read in-tree at the pre-fix revision e465e656be9cf5b69f6d100824d95fcd30c213a1^: (1) server/core.c:2269-2270 `methnum = ap_method_register(cmd->pool, apr_pstrdup(cmd->pool, method));` -- allocation site, size = strlen(method)+1 bump-allocated. (2) In .htaccess context cmd->pool IS the request pool: server/config.c:2174-2175 `parms.pool = r->pool; parms.temp_pool = r->pool;`. (3) register_one_method at modules/http/http_protocol.c:670 does `apr_hash_set(methods_registry, methname, APR_HASH_KEY_STRING, pnum)`. (4) APR's hash does NOT copy the key -- apr/tables/apr_hash.c:316 `he->key = key;` stores the caller's pointer verbatim. (5) methods_registry itself was created on the long-lived config pool: modules/http/http_protocol.c:685 `methods_registry = apr_hash_make(p)` called from register_hooks via modules/http/http_core.c:317, i.e. pconf. So a pconf-lifetime hash ends up holding a pointer into an r->pool allocation. (6) When the request ends r->pool is cleared/destroyed; per apr_pools.c:968 apr_pool_clear only rewinds first_avail and per apr_pools.c:458,469 the memnode is pushed onto the allocator freelist, NOT returned to free() (max_free_index defaults to APR_ALLOCATOR_MAX_FREE_UNLIMITED=0 at apr_pools.c:182, disabling the free()/munmap() branch at :486-489). The bytes are recycled to serve subsequent requests and are never scrubbed. (7) make_allow at modules/http/http_protocol.c:1023-1056 walks the registry (`apr_hash_first(r->pool, methods_registry)` :1027), pushes each dangling key into a pool array (:1040) and `apr_array_pstrcat(r->pool, allow, ',')` (:1056) strlen()s it into the response Allow: header. WHY THE POOL MAKES THIS READABLE RATHER THAN TRAPPING: there is no apr_pfree, so the string is never handed to an allocator that could unmap, poison, or quarantine it; the page stays mapped and writable for the whole process lifetime because the memnode is recycled forever. The dangling read therefore always succeeds, and it returns whatever request data was bump-allocated into those bytes afterwards -- which is precisely why the leak is of other users' request memory rather than a segfault. Under malloc+ASan/MTE the same dangling pointer would hit a quarantined/poisoned chunk and trap. Trunk fix is 4cc27823899e070268b906ca677ee838d07cf67a (svn r1807655); 2.4.x merge e465e656 (svn r1807754) is the released fix. The fix does not repair the lifetime, it forbids the registration: `if (cmd->pool == cmd->temp_pool) return apr_psprintf(...)` refuses method registration from .htaccess. Affected <= 2.4.27.

affected_function: ap_rgetline_core (consumed by ap_get_mime_headers_core / read_request_line via field_name_len)
trigger: Send an excessively long request header so LimitRequestFieldSize is hit, or make the read fail mid-line. Pre-fix, ap_rgetline_core returned early on several error paths (ap_get_brigade failure, empty brigade, apr_bucket_read failure, the CRLF-strictness path, and the obs-fold ENOSPC path) leaving the pool buffer un-NUL-terminated, and the buffer was allocated with no room for a terminator at all. The caller then logs the field with field_name_len(field), which runs ap_strchr_c(field, ':') over unterminated pool memory, reading past the end of the allocation.
notes: Affected 2.4.1-2.4.29 per the advisory; 'impractical to exploit with a production build and production LogLevel', because the out-of-bounds access is in the diagnostic logging path. Allocation site read at 073a2c47af^:server/protocol.c:297 -- `*s = apr_palloc(r->pool, current_alloc);` and :308 -- `new_buffer = apr_palloc(r->pool, new_size);` inside ap_rgetline_core(). SIZE EXPRESSIONS: current_alloc = len (first bucket length) and new_size = current_alloc*2 or (bytes_handled+len)*2 -- with NO slack for a NUL. That is exactly what the fix changes: both become `apr_palloc(r->pool, current_alloc + 1)` / `apr_palloc(r->pool, new_size + 1)`, all early `return rv;` sites become `goto cleanup;`, and the new cleanup block clamps `bytes_handled` to n-1 and always writes `(*s)[bytes_handled] = '\0';`. The out-of-bounds consumer read at 073a2c47af^:server/protocol.c:573-579 -- `static int field_name_len(const char *field) { const char *end = ap_strchr_c(field, ':'); ... }` -- called on the failure path at :973 (`(field) ? field_name_len(field) : 0` in the LimitRequestFieldSize APLOGNO(00561) message) and at :1035, and on the request line at :820-:871. VERDICT blind: the scan runs off a bump-allocated pool buffer into the adjacent objects of the same memnode, or into bytes left over from an earlier request on the same recycled memnode (apr_pool_clear rewinds first_avail without zeroing), with no per-object bounds event.

trigger: Code running inside an unprivileged child -- an in-process scripting interpreter such as mod_php, or any module/CGI that can write the process' own memory -- stores an arbitrary int into ap_scoreboard_image->parent[slot].bucket in the shared-memory scoreboard. The scoreboard is mapped read/write in every child. On the next graceful restart the ROOT parent re-forks that slot and passes the attacker's int straight through as an array index.
poc: https://github.com/cfreal/exploits/tree/master/CVE-2019-0211-apache
notes: Affects 2.4.17-2.4.38, unix MPMs prefork/worker/event. TWO arenas are involved and both are blind; alloc_arena records the arena of the object actually accessed out of bounds, which is a pool object. (a) CORRUPTION VECTOR = httpd-scoreboard-shm. server/scoreboard.c:132-143 (pre-fix rev c2eb8c657e^) computes scoreboard_size = sizeof(global_score) + sizeof(process_score)*server_limit + sizeof(worker_score)*server_limit*thread_limit, then scoreboard.c:184 (or :230 for the anonymous case) does one apr_shm_create(&ap_scoreboard_shm, scoreboard_size, fname, pool). ap_init_scoreboard (scoreboard.c:154-165) carves that single mapping by bare pointer bumps -- global, then parent[], then one worker_score row per child -- with NO per-slot header, no guard, no ownership bit and no bounds recorded anywhere; ap_get_scoreboard_process (scoreboard.c:690-696 at the same rev) range-checks only the slot INDEX, never the field values. Every child has the whole mapping writable, so process_score.bucket (an `int`, include/scoreboard.h:151 at the pre-fix rev) is fully attacker-controlled from an unprivileged child. Writing it is IN bounds -- the arena sees nothing wrong -- which is exactly why the defect is invisible until the parent uses the value. (b) OOB TARGETS = apr-pool. prefork: server/mpm/prefork/prefork.c:1207-1208 `all_buckets = apr_pcalloc(pconf, retained->mpm->num_buckets * sizeof(prefork_child_bucket));` -- allocation size is num_buckets (1 unless SO_REUSEPORT/ListenCoresBucketsRatio) * sizeof{pod,mutex,listeners}. prefork.c:979-980 the root parent reads the poisoned index back out of SHM (`make_child(ap_server_conf, child_slot, ap_get_scoreboard_process(child_slot)->bucket)`) and prefork.c:685 does `my_bucket = &all_buckets[bucket];` -- an unbounded index off a bump-allocated pool array, so my_bucket becomes an arbitrary address in (or past) pconf memory. prefork.c:432-434 then calls apr_proc_mutex_child_init(&my_bucket->mutex, apr_proc_mutex_lockfile(my_bucket->mutex), pchild), i.e. it dereferences that wild pointer and calls through the apr_proc_mutex method table found there -- and prefork.c:445 shows ap_run_drop_privileges() has NOT run yet, so the arbitrary call happens as root. That is the published exploit primitive. event MPM gives an OOB WRITE from the same poisoned value: server/mpm/event/event.c:2965 `retained->idle_spawn_rate[ps->bucket] = 1;` where event.c:3334 allocated `retained->idle_spawn_rate = (int *)apr_palloc(ap_pglobal, new_max * sizeof(int));` -- storing the constant 1 at an attacker-chosen int offset from a pool allocation, in the root parent. VERDICT blind: neither arena can see any of this. The scoreboard is one flat shm mapping with no per-slot metadata, so the poisoning write is indistinguishable from a legitimate MPM update; and apr_palloc/apr_pcalloc are pure bump pointers (apr_pools.c:846-847) that record no size and no redzone, so all_buckets[bucket] and idle_spawn_rate[bucket] resolve to whatever pconf/ap_pglobal object happens to sit at that offset -- a neighbouring pool object, not a fault. The fix deletes the stored value entirely: bucket = slot % num_buckets is recomputed in the parent from its own trusted slot number, and process_score.bucket is retained only as a documented-dead field.

trigger: A malformed request whose request-target parses to an EMPTY path, so apr_uri_parse leaves r->parsed_uri.path at NULL and later request processing dereferences it.
notes: CWE-476 per the CVE record fetched above; description verbatim: 'Malformed requests may cause the server to dereference a NULL pointer. This issue affects Apache HTTP Server 2.4.48 and earlier.' ORIGIN OF THE NULL, read in-tree: apr/uri/apr_uri.c:870-871 assigns the path only conditionally -- `if (s != uri) { uptr->path = apr_pstrmemdup(p, uri, s - uri); }` -- so a request-target with an empty path span leaves the field at the NULL written by the struct-wide `memset(uptr, '\0', sizeof(*uptr));` at apr_uri.c:840. The containing object is pool memory: `r = apr_pcalloc(p, sizeof(request_rec));` at 2.4.48:server/protocol.c:1272, on the request pool, and the path string when it IS assigned is an apr_pstrmemdup of size (s - uri) from that same pool. FIX_COMMIT DELIBERATELY LEFT EMPTY. The only candidate in the 2.4.48..2.4.49 range that adds the relevant guard is ecebcc035ccd8d0e2984fe41420d9e944f456b3c, which introduces `if (r->status == HTTP_OK && (r->parsed_uri.path != NULL) && ...)` in server/protocol.c -- but that commit is a bundled merge of THIRTEEN trunk revisions whose stated purpose is a refactor (splitting ap_create_request() from ap_read_request(), factoring ap_parse_request_line()/ap_check_request_header()), and the hunk adds new request-target validation that happens to contain a NULL guard rather than repairing an identifiable pre-existing dereference. Asserting it as the fix would be a guess, so the field is empty per the survey's rule that empty beats a guess; the candidate is recorded here instead. ARENA CAVEAT: a NULL dereference faults on the unmapped zero page under ANY allocator, so this row is not evidence of arena blindness the way the oob and use-after-free rows are; alloc_arena/verdict record where the containing object lived, not a missed detection. The arena-relevant observation is the same near miss as CVE-2026-33007: because apr_palloc has no failure or bounds event, a conditional-assignment field like parsed_uri.path is indistinguishable at runtime from a validly-initialised one. || VERDICT NORMALISED BY THIS SESSION: counted 'caught' because a NULL dereference is trapped by page protection on any hardware, independent of the allocator. It is NOT evidence that the arena is visible to CHERI, and it is NOT evidence of blindness either; it is excluded from the blind count on purpose so the headline figure stays conservative. alloc_arena still records the true origin of the object.

trigger: Any string containing the two-byte sequence backslash-quote is passed to ap_escape_quotes(). The sizing pass charges 2 bytes for an escaped pair and skips both, but the copy pass consumes the pair AND then falls through to the unguarded quote/char cases in the same iteration, emitting up to 4 bytes for 3 input bytes. One extra byte is written per '\"' occurrence. No in-tree module feeds untrusted data here; third-party modules and mod_lua scripts can.
notes: Affected <=2.4.48. Allocation site read at 2.4.48:server/util.c:2485 -- `outstring = apr_palloc(p, newlen + 1);` (same line 2537 in c69d4cc90c^ after unrelated churn). SIZE EXPRESSION: newlen + 1, where newlen adds 1 per input byte and 1 more per '"', and a backslash+X pair is charged 2 and skipped. Verified the mismatch by compiling the three real variants (2.4.48 `if`, the interim `while`, and the shipped fix) and brute-forcing every string over {'"','\\','a'} up to length 12: the 2.4.48 form overflows in 156315 cases (worst overrun 3 bytes at length 12, growing 1 byte per '\"' pair, so unbounded for longer input); the other two overflow in 0 cases. That zero is a meaningful zero because the same harness fires 156315 times on the vulnerable variant -- positive control. Note on the hash: commit c69d4cc90c (svn r1892012, 'fix ap_escape_quotes for pre-escaped quotes') is the commit that actually removes the overflow, by turning the leading `if` into a `while` so the pair-consuming branch cannot fall through. The later commit ac62c7e7436560cf4f7725ee586364ce95c07804 (svn r1892418, 'fix ap_escape_quotes substitution logic') restructures the loop into the shipped 2.4.49 form; its own pre-image already does not overflow, so it is a correctness follow-up, not the overflow fix. Both are inside the 2.4.48..2.4.49 range and the CHANGES security entry names only the release. VERDICT blind: outstring is a bump-pointer apr_palloc object with no header, no redzone and no size, so the extra bytes land on whatever pool object was allocated next inside the same memnode; no bounds event, no revocation, no scrub.

affected_function: ap_escape_html2 (reached with an oversized body admitted by ap_xml_parse_input / ap_get_limit_xml_body)
trigger: Set LimitXMLRequestBody to more than ~350 MB, or to 0, which pre-fix disabled the size check entirely (`if (limit_xml_body && total_read > limit_xml_body)` in server/util_xml.c). Then POST an XML body whose text is dominated by '"' (5 extra bytes each) or '&' (4 each) and get it echoed through ap_escape_html(). ap_escape_html2's counters are `int`, so `i + j` wraps past INT_MAX, apr_palloc gets a small or negative-turned-small size, and the second loop then memcpy()s the full escaped text past the end of the buffer. 350 MB * 6 > INT_MAX is the threshold in the advisory.
notes: Affected <=2.4.52. Allocation site read at 5a72f0fe6f^:server/util.c:2162 -- `x = apr_palloc(p, i + j + 1);` in ap_escape_html2(), declared `int i, j;` at :2145. SIZE EXPRESSION: i + j + 1 computed in `int`, where i counts input bytes and j accumulates +3 per '<' or '>', +4 per '&', +5 per '"' or per non-ASCII byte under toasc. The fix makes i and j apr_size_t and adds `if (i + j > APR_SIZE_MAX - 6) abort();` inside the counting loop; it also caps the directive at AP_MAX_LIMIT_XML_BODY = APR_SIZE_MAX/6 - 1 in server/core.c and makes LimitXMLRequestBody 0 mean that cap instead of 'no check'. The source of the oversized input is also pool memory: server/util_xml.c ap_xml_parse_input() creates the parser with `apr_xml_parser_create(r->pool)` and, pre-fix, skipped the length check whenever limit_xml_body was 0 (the `limit_xml_body &&` guard the fix deletes). VERDICT blind: the destination x is a bare bump-pointer apr_palloc object; the overflow writes forward through the rest of the memnode and into whatever the pool hands out next, with no per-object bounds event, no revocation and no scrub. Classed integer-overflow after the advisory's own wording; the memory-level event is an intra-arena overflow of a pool object.

trigger: Reflect a string of INT_MAX bytes or more with ap_rputs(). The inline wrapper computed `ap_rwrite(str, (int)strlen(str), r)`, so a size_t length > INT_MAX truncates to a negative int; ap_rwrite passed it straight to buffer_output(), whose parameter is apr_size_t, so the negative value sign-extends to a near-SIZE_MAX length. The output filter chain then reads that many bytes from the caller's buffer. Reachable from mod_lua's r:puts() with a ~2 GiB Lua string.
notes: CONTROL-GROUP ROW. Affected <=2.4.53. Bug sites read in 8c14927162^: `return ap_rwrite(str, (int)strlen(str), r);` in the static inline ap_rputs() at include/http_protocol.h:478, and `AP_DECLARE(int) ap_rwrite(const void *buf, int nbyte, request_rec *r)` at server/protocol.c:2129 which calls `buffer_output(r, buf, nbyte)` with no negative check; buffer_output's signature is `(request_rec *r, const char *str, apr_size_t len)` at server/protocol.c:2082-2083, so the sign extension happens at the call. The bogus length is then handed to `apr_bucket_transient_create(str, len, c->bucket_alloc)` at server/protocol.c:2100 -- that bucket DESCRIPTOR is apr-bucket-alloc memory, but the object actually read out of bounds is the caller's character buffer, which is why this row is not apr-bucket-alloc. The fix adds `if (nbyte < 0) return -1;` to ap_rwrite and makes ap_rputs loop in INT_MAX chunks. ALLOCATION SITE of the overread object, for the caller the advisory names: 8c14927162^:modules/lua/lua_request.c:517 -- `ap_rputs(luaL_checkstring(L, i), r);` inside req_puts() (r:puts). luaL_checkstring returns a pointer into a Lua string object, and mod_lua uses stock `luaL_newstate()` (modules/lua/lua_vmprep.c:339) with Lua's default realloc-based allocator => system-malloc. SIZE EXPRESSION: the Lua string's length, attacker-chosen and >= INT_MAX. There IS a pool-allocated variant of the same call in-tree -- modules/lua/mod_lua.c:108 `ap_rputs(ap_escape_html(r->pool, lua_response), r)`, whose argument comes from `apr_palloc(p, i + j + 1)` in ap_escape_html2 -- but that is a bounded error message, not attacker-drivable to 2 GiB, so system-malloc is the honest arena for this CVE. VERDICT caught, same caveat as CVE-2022-28615: the read runs off the end for gigabytes, so no allocator stops it on the first byte, but a malloc'd buffer is instrumentable (ASan/guard page) in a way an apr_palloc buffer is not.

trigger: Call ap_strcmp_match() with a subject string longer than INT_MAX. The cursors `x` and `y` are plain `int`, so after INT_MAX increments they wrap to INT_MIN and `str[x]` / `expected[y]` index roughly 2 GiB BEFORE the buffer. Reachable from a Lua script via r:strcmp_match() with a ~2 GiB string; the advisory states no code shipped with the server can be coerced into such a call.
notes: CONTROL-GROUP ROW. Affected <=2.4.53. Bug site read at 6503d09ab5^:server/util.c:188 -- `int x, y;` inside `AP_DECLARE(int) ap_strcmp_match(const char *str, const char *expected)` at :186; the fix changes both declarations to `apr_size_t`. ALLOCATION SITE of the object read out of bounds: the subject string is caller-owned. The only in-tree reachable caller is the mod_lua binding, read at 6503d09ab5^:modules/lua/lua_request.c:1709 -- `str = lua_tostring(L, 1);` inside lua_ap_strcmp_match() at :1702, which returns a pointer into a Lua string object. mod_lua creates its interpreters with plain `L = luaL_newstate();` (modules/lua/lua_vmprep.c:339, and modules/lua/mod_lua.c:1068) and never installs a pool-backed lua_Alloc, so Lua uses its default realloc/free allocator => system-malloc, NOT an APR pool. SIZE EXPRESSION: the Lua string's own length, attacker-chosen and > INT_MAX. The other in-tree callers (mod_autoindex, mod_file_cache, mod_ssl, mod_proxy) do pass apr-pool strings (r->uri, r->handler, config patterns) but none of those can reach 2 GiB, so no apr-pool row is justified here. VERDICT caught, with a caveat: the wrapped index lands ~2 GiB from the object, far outside any redzone, so a stock malloc gives no bounds event either -- what makes this 'caught' relative to the pool rows is that a malloc'd Lua heap is instrumentable at all (ASan shadow / guard pages / a hardened allocator will fault or report on the wild index), whereas an apr_palloc object carries no per-object metadata for any tool to check against.

trigger: A response carrying both r->content_languages entries and a Content-Language response header with tokens not already in the array (reachable via mod_mime language variants plus mod_headers setting Content-Language).
notes: Cleanest demonstration in the survey of an arena-specific failure mode: a stale-after-growth pointer that malloc would have turned into a freed-chunk access. Pre-fix modules/http/http_filters.c:1389 hoists `char **languages = (char **)(r->content_languages->elts);` OUT of the loop. Inside the loop, :1398 `*((char **) apr_array_push(r->content_languages)) = token;` can grow the array. apr_array_push (apr/tables/apr_tables.c) grows by allocating a NEW block -- `new_data = apr_palloc(arr->pool, arr->elt_size * new_size)` with new_size = nalloc*2 -- memcpy'ing, and assigning `arr->elts = new_data`. The OLD elts block is simply ABANDONED IN THE POOL: there is no apr_pfree, so it is neither freed nor poisoned and remains fully mapped and readable. The loop bound at :1393 is re-read each iteration (`i < r->content_languages->nelts`, which has grown) while `languages` still points at the old, smaller block, so `languages[i]` at :1394 reads past the end of the old allocation and ap_cstr_casecmp dereferences whatever pointer-shaped bytes follow it in the same memnode. Allocation size expression: elt_size * new_size = sizeof(char*) * (2 * nalloc). Fix moves the `languages` load inside the while loop so it is refreshed after every possible growth. Verdict blind: the stale block is live arena memory adjacent to other live objects, so there is no bounds event and no use-after-free event to detect -- under malloc/realloc the same pattern is a classic freed-pointer read that ASan and hardened allocators catch. Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.67.

trigger: A configuration file containing a crafted regular expression (LocationMatch / DirectoryMatch / FilesMatch / ProxyMatch) whose PCRE named-capture table entry has a first byte with the high bit set.
notes: Heap UNDERWRITE, i.e. a write before the start of a pool object -- in an arena that is a write into the neighbour allocated just before it, with nothing in between. Pre-fix server/util_pcre.c:524 `int capture = ((offset[0] << 8) + offset[1]);` where `const char *offset` is plain (signed on most targets) char. A name-table entry byte >= 0x80 sign-extends, so offset[0] << 8 is negative and `capture` is negative. The guard at :525 `while (names->nelts <= capture) apr_array_push(names);` never executes for a negative capture (nelts >= 0), so the code falls straight through to the indexed store at :529 `((char **) names->elts)[capture] = ...` (or :538 in the non-prefix branch) with a NEGATIVE index, writing a pointer below names->elts. Allocation site: the array is created by the caller at server/core.c:2528 `conf->refs = apr_array_make(cmd->pool, 8, sizeof(char *));` (also modules/proxy/mod_proxy.c:2888), and apr_array_make -> make_array_core -> apr/tables/apr_tables.c:73 `res->elts = apr_palloc(p, nelts * elt_size)`, so the backing store is a bare 8*sizeof(char*) = 64-byte bump allocation with no header, no redzone and no length. Verdict blind: the bytes below elts are another live pool object in the same memnode, so the write silently corrupts a neighbour rather than hitting allocator metadata or a guard page. Fix adds `if (capture > 1024) return -1;` and casts both bytes to unsigned char. Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.67.

trigger: Exhaust the Digest client-list shared memory -- default AuthDigestShmemSize is 1000 bytes, ~12 client entries -- by sending Digest requests from many distinct clients/opaque values. Once apr_rmm_malloc can no longer satisfy sizeof(client_entry), every subsequent request scribbles a client_entry over the RMM header block; the server then crashes on every request, including valid ones, until restarted.
notes: Affects 2.4.1-2.4.23. fix_commit is the trunk commit; the 2.4.x backport that shipped in 2.4.25 is d049e3ce42b89ba66c17b0cd8c4c5992ec2b12fe (both verified with git cat-file -t). Pre-fix revision read is 4354842828^. ARENA: this is NOT the pool allocator and NOT the httpd scoreboard -- it is APR's RMM (relocatable memory manager, apr-util misc/apr_rmm.c) layered over an apr_shm_t, classified here as httpd-scoreboard-shm per the survey's shared-memory-arena bucket, and it is an arena in its own right with no per-object redzone. Backing store: mod_auth_digest.c:180 `#define DEF_SHMEM_SIZE 1000L /* ~ 12 entries */`, :184 `static apr_size_t shmem_size = DEF_SHMEM_SIZE;` (settable by AuthDigestShmemSize, mod_auth_digest.c:673), then :252 `sts = apr_shm_create(&client_shm, shmem_size, NULL, ctx);` and :271-274 `apr_rmm_init(&client_rmm, ..., shmem_size, ctx);`. RMM carves that one mapping into rmm_block_t-prefixed blocks on used/free lists, with the single rmm_hdr_block_t pinned at offset 0 (apr_rmm.c:31-50, :52-67). ALLOCATION SITES of the object the bug touches: mod_auth_digest.c:834 and :843 `entry = apr_rmm_addr_get(client_rmm, apr_rmm_malloc(client_rmm, sizeof(client_entry)));` -- size expression sizeof(client_entry), where client_entry is the hash_entry at mod_auth_digest.c:114-119 (key, next, nonce_count, ha1[33], last_nonce[NONCE_LEN+1]). Same pattern at :280 (sizeof(*client_list) + sizeof(client_entry*)*num_buckets), :303 and :320. THE BUG: apr_rmm_malloc signals failure by returning offset 0 (apr_rmm.c:307-327: find_block_of_size returns 0, `this` stays 0), and apr_rmm_addr_get is a bare `return (void*)((char*)rmm->base + entity);` (apr_rmm.c:434-439). So on exhaustion the composition returns rmm->base -- NON-NULL -- and the `if (!entry)` guard at mod_auth_digest.c:835/844 CANNOT fire. add_client then initialises the returned pointer as a client_entry and links it (`entry->next = client_list->table[bucket];` mod_auth_digest.c:856), writing sizeof(client_entry) bytes over the RMM header block and into the first block's rmm_block_t {size,prev,next} metadata. The free/used lists are now garbage, so every later apr_rmm_malloc/apr_rmm_free walks corrupt offsets -- the advisory's 'continues to crash even for subsequently valid requests'. A second, independent defect in the same commit: gc() at mod_auth_digest.c:778-790 does `entry = client_list->table[idx]; while (entry->next)` with no NULL check, so an empty bucket is a plain null-deref (the fix adds `if (!entry) continue;`). VERDICT blind: RMM stores its block metadata inline, in the same shared mapping, with no canary and no allocator-side validation of the offset handed to apr_rmm_addr_get; offset 0 is simultaneously 'the header block' and 'the failure sentinel', a type confusion the arena has no way to detect. Nothing in the arena distinguishes a client_entry written at offset 0 from a legitimate allocation, and because the region is shared memory that is never unmapped, there is no fault at the moment of corruption -- only later, when the poisoned free list is walked.

trigger: Send `Authorization header Digest xxx` (or Proxy-Authorization) to a Digest-protected location, i.e. a first key token carrying NO '=' assignment. Repeat: the reflected bytes are whatever the previous request left in the same pool memnode.
notes: Affects 2.4.1-2.4.26 (and 2.2.0-2.2.33). Pre-fix revision read is 9a9867a40a^. ALLOCATION SITE: modules/aaa/mod_auth_digest.c:944-947 -- `l = strlen(auth_line); key = apr_palloc(r->pool, l+1); value = apr_palloc(r->pool, l+1);`. Allocation size expression = strlen(Authorization header remainder)+1, taken from the REQUEST POOL r->pool, via apr_palloc, which does not zero (only apr_pcalloc does). THE BUG: the parser at mod_auth_digest.c:966-994 only ever writes into `value` inside the `if (auth_line[0] == '=')` branch -- `vv = 0;` at :974 and `value[vv] = '\0';` at :993 are both INSIDE it. A key with no '=' therefore leaves `value` exactly as apr_palloc returned it, and mod_auth_digest.c:1003-1022 unconditionally does apr_pstrdup(r->pool, value) into resp->username / realm / nonce / uri / digest / cnonce / opaque / qop / nc. So apr_pstrdup strlen()s a buffer that was never written. Two distinct consequences, both from the same read: (1) the bytes are stale pool contents -- under apr_pool_clear the pool's memnodes are recycled with `active->first_avail = pool->self_first_avail` (apr_pools.c:968) and are NOT zeroed, and by default allocator_free only pushes memnodes onto allocator->free[index] (apr_pools.c:458,469) rather than calling free()/munmap(), because max_free_index defaults to APR_ALLOCATOR_MAX_FREE_UNLIMITED=0 (apr_pools.c:182) which disables that branch entirely -- so the reflected bytes are verbatim data from an EARLIER request served by the same child (headers, credentials, request bodies), echoed back in the log line and the 401 challenge. (2) if no NUL happens to lie within the l+1 bytes, the strlen runs past the allocation into the adjacent bump-allocated objects and off the end of the memnode -> segfault. Both are named in the advisory. VERDICT blind: apr_palloc is `mem = active->first_avail; active->first_avail += size;` (apr_pools.c:846-847) -- no header, no size, no initialised bit, no poison value, and no free path that could scrub -- so an uninitialised read of pool memory is bit-for-bit indistinguishable from a correct read, which is precisely why this reflected another request's data instead of tripping anything. A malloc arena would not have caught it either (malloc does not scrub), but a bump allocator makes the *previous tenant* of those exact bytes deterministic and adjacent, which is what turns 'uninitialised' into 'reliably discloses the last request'. The one-line fix hoists `vv = 0;` and `value[vv] = '\0';` out of the branch.

trigger: Threaded MPM (worker/event) with mod_auth_digest and two or more users authenticating concurrently against the same <Directory>/<Location>. Two requests in the same process race on the single shared conf->ha1 slot between the check_authn phase and the fixups phase.
notes: Affects 2.4.0-2.4.38, threaded MPMs only. JUDGEMENT CALL, stated explicitly: the advisory frames this purely as a race condition allowing a user with valid credentials to authenticate as another user, and the httpd CHANGES entry frames it as valid credentials being wrongly REFUSED. I include it because the underlying defect read in the source is a LIFETIME error, not only a data race, and the lifetime error is a use-after-free of pool memory. Pre-fix revision read is f01d50e83f^. THE OBJECT: the retrieved user:realm:password MD5 hash. ALLOCATION SITE: modules/aaa/mod_authn_file.c:151 `file_hash = ap_getword(r->pool, &rpw, ':');` returned via `*rethash = file_hash;` at mod_authn_file.c:161 -- a REQUEST-pool allocation, size = length of the password-file field + 1, bump-allocated out of r->pool. THE DEFECT: mod_auth_digest.c:1358-1360 `if (auth_result == AUTH_USER_FOUND) { conf->ha1 = password; }` parks that r->pool pointer in the per-directory config struct. That struct is built once at configuration time -- create_digest_dir_config(apr_pool_t *p, char *dir) at mod_auth_digest.c:455, i.e. pconf lifetime -- and is shared by EVERY thread in the process; `const char *ha1` was a member of digest_config_struct (removed by the fix). So a pconf-lifetime object holds a pointer into a per-request pool. Read-back sites: mod_auth_digest.c:1789 old_digest(r, resp, conf->ha1) and new_digest's `ha1 = conf->ha1;` (both in the check_authn hook, mod_auth_digest.c:1957), and critically mod_auth_digest.c:1904 `ha1 = conf->ha1;` inside add_auth_info, which is registered as ap_hook_fixups at mod_auth_digest.c:1960 -- i.e. read MUCH later in the request than it was written. Two failure modes fall out, and both are silent: (i) plain race -- thread B overwrites conf->ha1 between A's get_hash and A's read, so A computes/validates a digest against B's live hash (the advisory's cross-user authentication); (ii) use-after-free -- B's whole request can complete inside A's window, so B's r->pool is cleared/destroyed and A's later read at the fixups hook dereferences a pointer into a dead request pool. VERDICT blind, and (ii) is the reason this row is here: apr_pool_clear only rewinds `active->first_avail = pool->self_first_avail` (apr_pools.c:968) without zeroing, and apr_pool_destroy's memnodes go onto allocator->free[index] (apr_pools.c:458,469) rather than to free()/munmap(), because max_free_index defaults to APR_ALLOCATOR_MAX_FREE_UNLIMITED=0 (apr_pools.c:182). The freed bytes therefore stay mapped and readable forever, so the dangling read does not fault -- it returns either B's stale hash or whatever the recycled memnode now holds, i.e. it degrades into exactly the wrong-user-authenticates symptom rather than a crash. There is no revocation, no scrub and no quarantine that could turn it into an observable event. The fix moves ha1 into digest_header_rec (`const char *ha1;`), which lives in r->request_config, restoring per-request lifetime AND per-thread ownership in one move -- note that the same edit fixes both the race and the dangling pointer, which is the tell that they are one defect.

trigger: Send an Authorization header Digest header whose nonce is exactly NONCE_LEN characters and whose first NONCE_TIME_LEN (12) characters are all valid base64 alphabet with NO '=' padding, e.g. nonce="AAAAAAAAAAAA<40 hex>". Genuine nonces always carry '=' at index 11, which is what normally keeps the decode inside the buffer.
notes: CONTROL-GROUP ROW. Affects 2.4.0-2.4.46. Pre-fix revision read is 3b6431eb9c^. STACK BUFFER, NOT HEAP -- alloc_arena is set to system-malloc per the survey convention, but nothing was malloc'd or palloc'd: the destination is the automatic variable at modules/aaa/mod_auth_digest.c:1426 `time_rec nonce_time;`, whose type is the union at mod_auth_digest.c:162-165 `typedef union time_union { apr_time_t time; unsigned char arr[sizeof(apr_time_t)]; } time_rec;`. Size expression = sizeof(apr_time_t) = 8 bytes, fixed at compile time, in check_nonce's frame alongside `char tmp, hash[NONCE_HASH_LEN+1];`. THE BUG: mod_auth_digest.c:104-106 give NONCE_TIME_LEN = ((sizeof(apr_time_t)+2)/3)*4 = 12 and NONCE_LEN = 12 + 2*APR_SHA1_DIGESTSIZE. check_nonce validates only the total LENGTH (mod_auth_digest.c:1429 `if (strlen(resp->nonce) != NONCE_LEN)`), then mod_auth_digest.c:1437-1439 truncates the nonce to its first 12 chars and calls `apr_base64_decode_binary(nonce_time.arr, resp->nonce);`. In apr/encoding/apr_base64.c:174-192 the decoder derives nprbytes by scanning to the first non-base64 character and emits 3 bytes per full 4-character group. A server-generated nonce ends its time field with '=' (the encoder emits it at apr_base64.c:250), so nprbytes = 11 -> 2 full groups (6 bytes) + the tail at :195-202 (2 more) = exactly 8. An attacker-supplied nonce with 12 unpadded base64 characters gives nprbytes = 12 -> 3 full groups = 9 bytes written into the 8-byte arr: one byte past the end, and its value is pr2six[c3]<<6 | pr2six[c4], which the attacker can make zero -- the advisory's 'single byte, zero byte' overflow. VERDICT caught, and the reasoning matters because it is the opposite of every other row here: the object's extent is a compile-time constant on the stack, so it is exactly the case bounds enforcement can see. ASan's stack redzones, a bounds-checking or capability-based toolchain (which narrows a stack allocation to its declared object), or a fat-pointer discipline all trap on the 9th byte. What would NOT catch it is a plain stack canary: nonce_time is a local among other locals, so the extra byte lands inside the same frame -- on hash[] or on padding -- and never reaches the canary. That is consistent with the advisory's own note that no exploitable instance could be produced. This row is the control: had the same 8-byte object been bump-allocated from an APR pool, the 9th byte would have landed in the neighbouring pool object with nothing to observe it, i.e. it would have been 'blind' like the rest. The fix rejects the nonce up front, adding `|| resp->nonce[NONCE_TIME_LEN - 1] != '='` to the length check.

trigger: A request in a caching FORWARD PROXY configuration whose r->uri contains no '/' at all (absolute-URI or authority-form request target), with AuthnCacheContext set to the special value 'directory'.
notes: Worth recording despite being classed a NULL deref, because the mechanism is an ALLOCATION SIZE computed from a NULL pointer, and the arena's behaviour is what decides whether it crashes or corrupts. Pre-fix modules/aaa/mod_authn_socache.c:273 `char *slash = strrchr(r->uri, '/');` with no NULL check -- the source even carried the comment `/* FIXME: are we at risk of this blowing up? */`. When r->uri has no slash, slash is NULL and :274 computes `apr_palloc(r->pool, slash - r->uri + strlen(r->server->server_hostname) + 1)`, i.e. a pointer difference against NULL, which converts to an enormous apr_size_t. The subsequent `strcpy(new_context, r->server->server_hostname)` then dereferences the failed (NULL) allocation. Allocation size expression: (slash - r->uri) + strlen(server_hostname) + 1. VERDICT REASONING, and this is the honest caveat: a NULL dereference traps on the unmapped zero page under ANY allocator, so this row is NOT evidence of arena blindness in the way the oob and use-after-free rows are -- it is marked blind only because the object is pool memory. The genuinely arena-relevant observation is the near miss: the bug survives only because the bogus size is ABSURD. Had the wild pointer difference produced a merely-too-small plausible size, apr_palloc would have satisfied it silently from the bump pointer with no failure to check, and the strcpy would have overflowed into the neighbouring pool object instead of crashing -- the same shape as CVE-2026-34356 in this survey. Fix hoists the strrchr and adds `&& slash` to the branch condition. Affects 2.4.66 and earlier. || VERDICT NORMALISED BY THIS SESSION: counted 'caught' because a NULL dereference is trapped by page protection on any hardware, independent of the allocator. It is NOT evidence that the arena is visible to CHERI, and it is NOT evidence of blindness either; it is excluded from the blind count on purpose so the headline figure stays conservative. alloc_arena still records the true origin of the object.

trigger: With AuthLDAPCharsetConfig configured, send a request with an Accept-Language header value shorter than three characters -- e.g. `Accept-Language: e`, or an empty value -- to an mod_authnz_ldap-protected location. The value misses the charset table, so the fallback truncation runs on a buffer that is too short to hold it.
notes: Affects 2.4.1-2.4.29, only when AuthLDAPCharsetConfig is set. Pre-fix revision read is ed789bf5c1^. ALLOCATION SITE: modules/aaa/mod_authnz_ldap.c:148 `lang_line = apr_pstrdup(r->pool, lang_line);` where lang_line came from `apr_table_get(r->headers_in, "accept-language")` at mod_authnz_ldap.c:143. Allocation size expression = strlen(Accept-Language value)+1 bytes, bump-allocated from the request pool (apr_pstrdup = strlen+1 then apr_palloc then memcpy). mod_authnz_ldap.c:149-154 then truncates the copy IN PLACE at the first ',' or ';' -- note this writes a NUL inside the buffer but does not shrink the allocation, so the exploitable case needs the whole header value to be short, not just its first token. THE BUG: mod_authnz_ldap.c:127 misses the charset hash, and the fallback at mod_authnz_ldap.c:129-131 does `if (!charset) { language[2] = '\0'; ... }` with no length check at all. For `Accept-Language: e` the allocation is 2 bytes and the write at index 2 is one byte past the end; for an empty header value the allocation is 1 byte and it is two bytes past. VERDICT blind: the target is a bump-allocated pool string. apr_palloc hands out `mem = active->first_avail; active->first_avail += size;` (apr_pools.c:846-847) with no header, no length and no redzone, and there is no apr_pfree that could ever validate a size, so the stray NUL simply overwrites the first byte(s) of whatever object the request pool bump-allocated next -- typically another header copy or an internal struct field. Nothing faults, nothing is recorded; the corruption surfaces later as a mangled string or a mis-parsed struct somewhere unrelated, which is why the advisory can only say 'a memory location that is not part of the string'. Contrast the CVE-2020-35452 row: the identical one-byte-NUL write into a fixed-size STACK object is statically bounded and catchable, while here the allocation size is a runtime function of an attacker-chosen header length and the arena keeps no record of it. The fix replaces the in-place truncation with `if (!charset && strlen(language) > 3 && language[2] == '-') { char *language_short = apr_pstrndup(p, language, 2); ... }` -- both a length guard and a fresh allocation instead of a destructive write.

trigger: With mod_cache + mod_cache_socache enabled, get a response cached whose serialised header block contains a header with an empty value, i.e. `Name:` followed directly by CRLF. On the next cache hit the whitespace-skip loop walks over the '\r' and past the end of the entry.
notes: Affects 2.4.6-2.4.29, mod_cache_socache only. Pre-fix revision read is c327f16fbb^. ALLOCATION SITE: modules/cache/mod_cache_socache.c:464-467 -- `apr_pool_create(&sobj->pool, r->pool); sobj->buffer = apr_palloc(sobj->pool, dconf->max); sobj->buffer_len = dconf->max;`. Allocation size expression = dconf->max, the CacheSocacheMaxSize directive (default 102400), bump-allocated from a child pool of the request pool (the same pattern at mod_cache_socache.c:810 on the store path). The socache retrieve fills the first buffer_len bytes of it; buffer_len is the retrieved entry length and is strictly less than sobj->buffer_len (checked at mod_cache_socache.c:565). read_table is then called on it twice, mod_cache_socache.c:636 and :642, sharing a `slider` offset. THE BUG: mod_cache_socache.c:216-218 `while (apr_isspace(buffer[colon])) { colon++; }` -- apr_isspace('\r') is TRUE, so for a header with nothing between the ':' and the CRLF the loop steps over the '\r', over the '\n', and keeps going through the rest of the entry and then past buffer_len entirely, bounded by nothing (the enclosing loop's `*slider < buffer_len` guard is on slider, not on colon). Two consequences: colon runs off the end of the meaningful data, and because colon can now exceed *slider, the very next statement mod_cache_socache.c:219-221 `apr_table_addn(table, apr_pstrndup(r->pool, buffer + key, len - key), apr_pstrndup(r->pool, buffer + colon, *slider - colon));` computes `*slider - colon` as an apr_size_t UNDERFLOW -- a near-SIZE_MAX length handed to apr_pstrndup, which then memchr's for a NUL across the whole address space. That is the crash the advisory reports as a DoS. VERDICT blind: sobj->buffer is a plain apr_palloc bump allocation (apr_pools.c:846-847) with no size header, no redzone and no free-side validation, so walking colon past dconf->max simply reads the neighbouring objects in the same memnode -- and the cached headers of OTHER responses, since the socache entry was copied into pool memory. The eventual segfault comes only from running off the end of the memnode's mmap, i.e. from the OS, not from the arena. The fix bounds the loop: `while (apr_isspace(buffer[colon]) && (colon < *slider))`, with the comment 'Do not go past the \r from above as apr_isspace('\r') is true'.

trigger: A request whose URI has no path segment, so apr_uri_parse() leaves apr_uri_t.path NULL. For mod_dav: a WebDAV method carrying a tagged If: header such as 'If: <http://host> (<locktoken>)' -- dav_process_if_header() calls ap_getparents(parsed_uri.path) on the NULL. For mod_cache: a request line like 'GET http://host HTTP/1.1' when CacheIgnoreURLSessionIdentifiers is configured -- cache_generate_key_default() calls strrchr(path, ';') on the NULL.
notes: Borderline call, reasoning stated. Affects 2.0.35-2.0.63 and 2.2.0-2.2.15 (mod_dav on 2.0 and 2.2, mod_cache on 2.2 only). Deref sites read at 98115eef19^:modules/dav/main/util.c:635-638 ('ap_getparents(parsed_uri.path); uri_len = strlen(parsed_uri.path); ... parsed_uri.path[--uri_len]') and 98115eef19^:modules/cache/cache_storage.c:482 + :498 ('path = r->parsed_uri.path;' then 'if ((param = strrchr(path, ';'))'). The whole apr_uri_t is zeroed first by 'memset(uptr, '\0', sizeof(*uptr));' at apr_uri.c:840, and the assignment at :871 is guarded by 'if (s != uri)' at :870, so an empty path leaves the field at its memset NULL and no allocation happens at all. Verdict caught: when the path is present it is ordinary bump-allocated pool memory with no bounds, but the fault here is a load from a NULL pointer, which the MMU traps at page zero regardless of allocator. No arena object's bounds are violated, so this row does not demonstrate arena blindness -- it is listed for completeness of the cluster. VERDICT NORMALISED IN MERGE: this row was submitted as `caught`, reasoned (correctly) from the fault being taken on the zero page. It is recorded as `blind` so that the verdict column stays a mechanical function of alloc_arena across the whole survey; the detection here comes from the MMU, not from the allocator, exactly as the caveat above says. || VERDICT NORMALISED BY THIS SESSION: counted 'caught' because a NULL dereference is trapped by page protection on any hardware, independent of the allocator. It is NOT evidence that the arena is visible to CHERI, and it is NOT evidence of blindness either; it is excluded from the blind count on purpose so the headline figure stays conservative. alloc_arena still records the true origin of the object.

trigger: Send a DAV request (e.g. a PROPPATCH/LOCK/WRITE body) whose XML CDATA begins with whitespace, so the strip_white path runs. The leading-whitespace loop advances the `cdata` pointer without decrementing `len`, so the subsequent trailing-whitespace scan indexes cdata[len] up to k bytes past the end of the len+1 buffer (k = number of leading whitespace bytes) and the final `cdata[len + 1] = '\0';` writes k+1 bytes past the end.
notes: Affected 2.4.1-2.4.8 (and 2.2.x through 2.2.27). Allocation site read at 771d2e83a6^:modules/dav/main/util.c:377 -- `cdata = s = apr_palloc(pool, len + 1);` in dav_xml_get_cdata(); pool is the request pool at every in-tree call site. SIZE EXPRESSION: len + 1, where len is the summed strlen() of every apr_text cdata fragment of the element and its children (accumulated at :351 and :360). Bug sites read at :399-400 (`while (apr_isspace(*cdata)) ++cdata;` with no --len), :403 (`while (len-- > 0 && apr_isspace(cdata[len])) continue;` -- the out-of-bounds READ) and :405 (`cdata[len + 1] = '\0';` -- the out-of-bounds WRITE). The fix is exactly `--len;` added to the leading-whitespace loop. Overrun is bounded by k <= len, so it stays a short forward overrun into the same or the next pool memnode rather than a wild write, hence intra-arena-overflow rather than oob-write. fixed_in: the CHANGES security entry sits under 'Changes with Apache 2.4.9' and the CVE record says 'before 2.4.8'; the 2.4.x backport commit 771d2e83a6 is already contained in the 2.4.8 tag, which was superseded by 2.4.9. Trunk commit is 02780d57bd9287c472c9ce5c25c6e46d04d67ea6 (identical diff, same line numbers). VERDICT blind: apr_palloc hands out a header-less bump-pointer slice, so both the read and the NUL write land on the neighbouring pool object with no bounds check, no revocation and nothing to trap on.

trigger: With mod_dav loaded and configured, send a WebDAV request carrying an If: header whose list contains an 'N' that is not followed by 'ot' and that sits at or near the end of the value -- e.g. `If: (N)`. The 'N' case advances the cursor by 2 unconditionally, stepping over the terminating NUL.
notes: CVE id is a 2006-block id assigned in 2023; affects 2.4.0-2.4.54 (mod_dav only). Pre-fix revision read is 7469547c3f^. ALLOCATION SITE: modules/dav/main/util.c:686 `if ((str = apr_pstrdup(r->pool, apr_table_get(r->headers_in, "If"))) == NULL) return NULL;` -- allocation size expression = strlen(If: header value)+1, bump-allocated from the request pool. Everything else in the parser points INTO this one buffer: dav_fetch_next_token (util.c:642-658) returns `tok = *str + 1` and sets `*str = sp`, so the `list` cursor at util.c:744 is an interior pointer into the same apr_pstrdup allocation. THE BUG: util.c:794-806, `case 'N': if (list[1] == 'o' && list[2] == 't') { ... condition = DAV_IF_COND_NOT; } list += 2; break;` -- the `list += 2` was OUTSIDE the if. Two violations follow. (1) OOB READ: when the 'N' is the last character, list[1] is the terminating NUL and list[2] is already one byte past the allocation; and since `list += 2` (plus the `list++` at util.c:823) steps the cursor past the NUL, the enclosing `while (*list)` at util.c:760 keeps parsing adjacent pool bytes -- an unbounded walk through whatever the request pool bump-allocated after the header copy. (2) WRITE OF A SINGLE ZERO BYTE: if that walk meets a '<' or '[', dav_fetch_next_token is called on out-of-bounds memory and util.c:655 `*sp = '\0';` stores a NUL wherever the matching '>' or ']' happened to be found -- past the end of the header value, exactly as the advisory describes ('a memory read, or write of a single zero byte, in a pool (heap) memory location beyond the header value sent'). VERDICT blind: the buffer is a bump-allocated pool string with no header, no recorded length and no redzone (apr_palloc, apr_pools.c:846-847), and pool objects are adjacent inside the memnode with no gap, so both the walk and the NUL store land on live neighbouring pool objects rather than on unmapped memory. The crash the advisory mentions only happens if the walk eventually runs off the END of the memnode -- i.e. the observable event depends on where in the memnode the header copy happened to land, not on the violation itself. The fix turns the fallthrough into an error: the `list += 2` moves inside the successful branch and an else returns DAV_ERR_IF_UNK_CHAR.

trigger: Open and close many HTTP/2 connections under load. h2_mplx_release_and_join() aborts the mplx and unregisters it, then the session pool holding the h2_mplx is destroyed; a worker thread that had already pulled that h2_mplx* out of the workers fifo (fifo_peek released the fifo lock BEFORE invoking the callback) then calls h2_mplx_pop_task() on it.
notes: Affects 2.4.26; fixed in 2.4.27. The fix commit names the CVE. Object: h2_mplx *m (the per-connection multiplexer). Allocation site read at modules/http2/h2_mplx.c:164 (rev a9067ba9f7^): 'm = apr_pcalloc(parent, sizeof(h2_mplx));' - allocation size expression sizeof(h2_mplx). 'parent' is session->pool, passed at modules/http2/h2_session.c:817 ('session->mplx = h2_mplx_create(c, session->pool, ...)'). The two halves of the fix are (a) h2_util.c fifo_peek() now calls fn(elem, ctx) while still holding fifo->lock instead of after unlocking, and (b) h2_mplx.c drops the second, post-join h2_workers_unregister() (the workaround that had been racing). Verdict blind: session->pool is a plain APR pool; when it is destroyed the h2_mplx bytes go back onto allocator->free[] (apr_pools.c:458,469) and are never munmap'd by default (APR_ALLOCATOR_MAX_FREE_UNLIMITED at apr_pools.c:182), so the worker's reads of m->lock / m->aborted / m->q hit mapped, recycled arena memory - no fault, no allocator metadata to check.

trigger: Any HTTP/2 stream that reaches destruction: h2_stream_destroy() destroys the pool the h2_stream itself was allocated from and then writes NULL into the (now freed) struct field stream->pool.
notes: Affects 2.4.17-2.4.29; fixed in 2.4.33 (the CHANGES entry sits in the unreleased 2.4.30 block). Advisory wording: 'could have written a NULL pointer potentially to an already freed memory' - this is a write-after-free, hence bug_class use-after-free. Object: h2_stream *stream. Allocation site read at modules/http2/h2_stream.c:545 (rev cc19d3ca86^): 'h2_stream *stream = apr_pcalloc(pool, sizeof(h2_stream));' - allocation size expression sizeof(h2_stream). The pool is the dedicated per-stream pool created at modules/http2/h2_session.c:133 ('apr_pool_create(&stream_pool, session->pool); apr_pool_tag(stream_pool, "h2_stream")'). Verdict blind: apr_pstrndup is a bump allocation inside a memnode of the per-stream pool (no header, no size, no free bit); after the stream pool is cleared/destroyed the bytes are recycled but stay mapped, so the strcmp reads whatever request now occupies them - which is why the advisory says the request is 'processed incorrectly' rather than crashing.

affected_function: h2_push_collect (modules/http2/h2_push.c), on an h2_headers beamed by h2_bucket_headers_beam (h2_headers.c)

affected_function: h2_session_stream_get / on_frame_recv_cb / on_stream_close_cb (modules/http2/h2_session.c), reading nghttp2's stream_user_data

affected_function: out_open / out_close / task_done / stream_destroy_iter (modules/http2/h2_mplx.c) logging on m->c instead of task->c
trigger: Trace/debug logging enabled for mod_http2 plus concurrent streams: mplx functions that run on a secondary (worker) thread emit ap_log_cerror()/h2_beam_log() against m->c, the MASTER connection, so the worker thread allocates from the master connection's apr_pool_t at the same time the master thread does.
notes: Affects 2.4.20-2.4.43. Fix commit is messaged as 'mod_http2: connection terminology renamed to master/secondary' (svn r1878926 + r1879156) but is in substance a thread-ownership audit: it prefixes every mplx function with m_/s_/t_/mst_ for the thread it runs on and switches the offending log statements from m->c to task->c / stream->task->c. Located by 'git log -S' on the changed lines, which returns exactly this commit in the 2.4.43..2.4.46 range. Object: the connection log-id string. Allocation site read at server/log.c:890 (rev 63a0a87efa^), in core_generate_log_id(): 'encoded = apr_palloc(r ? r->pool : c->pool, len);' - allocation size expression len = apr_base64_encode_len(sizeof(apr_uint64_t)) = 13 bytes; with r == NULL the pool is the MASTER conn_rec's c->pool. Reached from log_error_core at server/log.c:1199-1200 ('if (c && !c->log_id) add_log_id(c, NULL);'), i.e. on the first ap_log_cerror() against that connection. Log message formatting itself uses a stack buffer (errstr[MAX_STRING_LEN]), so this apr_palloc plus the unsynchronised store to c->log_id is the concurrent pool use the advisory names. Verdict blind: apr_palloc is an unlocked bump ('mem = active->first_avail; active->first_avail += size;', apr_pools.c:846-847), so two threads racing on the same pool can be handed overlapping bytes or leave first_avail past node->endp; there is no allocator metadata that could notice. This is the only row in the cluster whose defect is a data race rather than a single-threaded violation - classified intra-arena-overflow because the observable corruption is one arena object written over another.

affected_function: move_to_last / h2_push_diary_append (modules/http2/h2_push.c), reached from h2_push_diary_update after h2_push_diary_digest_set

trigger: An HTTP/2 request whose VERY FIRST header violates a size limit (pseudo-header longer than LimitRequestLine), or a violating header sent in a footer/trailer: h2_stream_add_header() jumps to cleanup before stream->rtmp is ever created, and set_error_response() writes through it.
