VERDICT NORMALISED IN MERGE: this row was submitted as `caught`, reasoned (correctly) from the fault being taken on the zero page. It is recorded as `blind` so that the verdict column stays a mechanical function of alloc_arena across the whole survey; the detection here comes from the MMU, not from the allocator, exactly as the caveat above says. || VERDICT NORMALISED BY THIS SESSION: counted 'caught' because a NULL dereference is trapped by page protection on any hardware, independent of the allocator. It is NOT evidence that the arena is visible to CHERI, and it is NOT evidence of blindness either; it is excluded from the blind count on purpose so the headline figure stays conservative. alloc_arena still records the true origin of the object.

trigger: An HTTP/2 client resets a stream early, so the stream reaches both the 'joined' and the 'cleanup' paths and is queued for purging twice.
notes: Double free at POOL granularity rather than object granularity, which is what makes it an arena bug. Pre-fix modules/http2/h2_mplx.c pushes the same h2_stream* onto the purge array from three different sites with no membership test: :134 (c1c2_stream_joined), :167 and :183 (m_stream_cleanup), each `APR_ARRAY_PUSH(m->spurge, h2_stream *) = stream;`. The purge loop at :604-605 iterates m->spurge and destroys each entry, so a stream present twice is destroyed twice. Destroy means h2_stream_destroy at modules/http2/h2_stream.c:635 `apr_pool_destroy(stream->pool);` -- so the second pass calls apr_pool_destroy on an already-destroyed pool, corrupting the allocator free-list that the first destroy pushed the memnodes onto (apr_pools.c:458,469). Allocation sites: the stream itself modules/http2/h2_stream.c:585 `h2_stream *stream = apr_pcalloc(pool, sizeof(h2_stream));` with stream->pool = pool at :592; the purge array modules/http2/h2_mplx.c:309 `m->spurge = apr_array_make(m->pool, 10, sizeof(h2_stream*));`. Verdict blind, with a telling detail: mod_http2 hand-rolled its OWN sentinel for exactly this class -- H2_STRM_ASSERT_MAGIC / H2_STRM_ASSIGN_MAGIC(stream, H2_STRM_MAGIC_SDEL) at h2_stream.c:631,634 -- because the pool provides no use-after-free or double-free detection whatsoever. That sentinel is itself unreliable here, because after the first apr_pool_destroy the struct's bytes return to the allocator free-list and can be handed out and overwritten before the second pass reads the magic. Fix adds a linear add_for_purge() membership check before every push. Affects 2.4.66. Advisory notes possible RCE.

trigger: An HTTP/2 upload request when the server has exhausted its file descriptors, so apr_file_pipe_create_pools fails after the beam callbacks have already been registered.
notes: Error-path lifetime bug: callbacks outlive the context they close over. Pre-fix modules/http2/h2_mplx.c:883-885 registers three beam callbacks on the LONG-LIVED stream->input beam with the SHORT-LIVED c2 connection (and stream) as their context -- `h2_beam_on_send(stream->input, c2_beam_input_write_notify, c2)`, `h2_beam_on_received(..., c2)`, `h2_beam_on_consumed(..., stream)` -- and only THEN attempts the fallible `apr_file_pipe_create_pools(..., c2->pool, c2->pool)` at :888-891, whose failure does `goto cleanup` at :892. The cleanup label at :899 returns the error without unregistering anything, so the beam keeps three callbacks pointing at a c2 whose pool is then destroyed. Any later activity on that beam invokes them against recycled memory. Allocation site: modules/http2/h2_c2.c:834 `c2 = (conn_rec *) apr_palloc(pool, sizeof(conn_rec));` on a dedicated pool created at :831 `apr_pool_create(&pool, parent)` (tagged h2_c2_conn at :832), reached from modules/http2/h2_mplx.c:940 `c2 = h2_c2_create(m->c1, transit->pool, transit->bucket_alloc);`. Allocation size expression: apr_palloc(pool, sizeof(conn_rec)). Verdict blind: on pool destruction the conn_rec's memnodes are recycled onto the allocator free-list rather than unmapped (apr_pools.c:458,469; the free()/munmap() branch at :486-489 is disabled by the default max_free_index = 0 at apr_pools.c:182), so the stale callback context stays mapped and the callback runs against whatever now occupies those bytes instead of faulting. Fix moves the three registrations to AFTER the pipe creation succeeds. Note the fix commit is a bundled mod_http2 2.0.39-2.0.42 update; the hunk above (h2_mplx.c c2_setup_io reordering) is the one corresponding to the 2.0.40 entry 'left beam bucket callbacks in place, potentially using no longer valid references'. Affects 2.4.55 through 2.4.67.

trigger: On Windows with mod_isapi, a request to an ISAPI .dll that fails in ap_setup_client_block() (e.g. a malformed chunked/Content-Length body) or whose body read returns an error takes the error path 'isapi_unload(isa, 0); return res;'. isapi_unload() calls apr_dso_unload(isa->handle) (FreeLibrary) but the cached isapi_loaded entry keeps its GetExtensionVersion / HttpExtensionProc / TerminateExtension function pointers into the now-unmapped image, and isapi_lookup() returns that cached entry to the next request without re-checking isa->handle. The next request then calls through the dangling pointer.
notes: CONTROL-GROUP row, and a borderline one -- reasoning stated explicitly. Affects 2.0.37-2.0.63 and 2.2.0-2.2.14 (2.0.x fix is 82376adb3ec3b274b5fd7ce7f3980bede25f1d0d). Sites read at 56b1703293^:modules/arch/win32/mod_isapi.c:1506 and :1537 (the two premature 'isapi_unload(isa, 0);' calls the fix deletes), :239 ('apr_dso_unload(isa->handle); isa->handle = NULL;' -- note it clears only handle, not the three function pointers declared at :215-217), :271 ('rv = apr_dso_load(&isa->handle, isa->filename, p);'), :338-356 (isapi_lookup returns the cached entry on last_load_rv == APR_SUCCESS with no handle check), and the dangling call itself at :1584 ('rv = (*isa->HttpExtensionProc)(cid->ecb);'). The memory that is actually released is a DSO image mapping torn down by apr_dso_unload -> FreeLibrary; it is neither apr_palloc'd nor malloc'd, so alloc_arena is recorded as system-malloc to mean NOT-the-arena rather than literally malloc. The struct HOLDING the stale pointers is pool memory: 'apr_pcalloc(loaded.pool, sizeof(isapi_loaded))' at mod_isapi.c:423, size sizeof(isapi_loaded) (~11 words), in the module-global loaded.pool -- that struct is never freed and is not the lifetime bug. Verdict caught: an OS-level unmap is a real revocation, so the indirect call through the orphaned pointer faults deterministically unless another module is later loaded at the same base -- which is exactly the 'potentially allow arbitrary code execution' caveat in the advisory. This is the opposite of the arena case, where nothing is ever unmapped.

trigger: mod_ldap used with LDAPTrustedClientCert in a per-directory context; a cached LDAP connection outlives the per-directory config pool it borrowed the certificate array from.
notes: A pure pool-LIFETIME use-after-free: no bug in any single function, only two objects with different pool lifetimes joined by an aliasing helper. Pre-fix modules/ldap/util_ldap.c:900 `l->client_certs = apr_array_copy_hdr(l->pool, dc->client_certs);` The name is the trap: apr_array_copy_hdr copies only the HEADER and ALIASES the element storage -- apr/tables/apr_tables.c:196 `res->elts = arr->elts;` (via copy_array_hdr_core, called from apr_array_copy_hdr at :210). So although the header is allocated on the long-lived connection pool l->pool (apr/tables/apr_tables.c:208 `apr_palloc(p, sizeof(apr_array_header_t))`), the elements -- and the path and password strings they point at -- remain owned by the per-directory config pool dc. The cached connection is reused after that config pool is cleared, so the TLS client certificate paths and passwords are read out of recycled pool bytes. Verdict blind: apr_pool_clear rewinds first_avail (apr_pools.c:968) without zeroing and the memnode is recycled rather than freed (apr_pools.c:458,469; the free()/munmap() branch at :486-489 is disabled by the default max_free_index = APR_ALLOCATOR_MAX_FREE_UNLIMITED = 0 at apr_pools.c:182), so the stale read always succeeds and silently returns another request's bytes as a certificate path. Fix switches to apr_array_copy (which really copies the elements, apr/tables/apr_tables.c) and additionally apr_pstrdup's each .path and .password onto l->pool. Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.67. Contrast with CVE-2017-9798, which is the same aliasing mistake reached through apr_hash_set instead.

trigger: With a %{name}C log format configured, send a Cookie: header whose last (or only) token is truncated -- a bare name with no '=' assignment, e.g. `Cookie: foo`. apr_strtok returns the token, and `value = name + strlen(name) + 1` then points one byte PAST the terminating NUL of the pstrdup'd copy. strlen(value) scans on into adjacent pool bytes, and the trailing-whitespace loop writes '\0' into them. Advisory reports a segmentation fault and child crash.
notes: Affected 2.4.1-2.4.8 (and 2.2.x). Allocation site read at 9e659703d4^:modules/loggers/mod_log_config.c:542 -- `char *cookies = apr_pstrdup(r->pool, cookies_entry);` where cookies_entry is apr_table_get(r->headers_in, "Cookie") (:540). SIZE EXPRESSION: apr_pstrdup allocates strlen(Cookie header value) + 1 via apr_palloc on r->pool. Bug sites read at :547 -- `char *value = name + strlen(name) + 1;` (one past the buffer's own NUL when the token is the last and contains no '='), :553 -- `last = value + strlen(value) - 1;` (the out-of-bounds READ), and :554-557 -- `while (last >= value && apr_isspace(*last)) { *last = '\0'; --last; }` (an out-of-bounds WRITE of NUL bytes over any trailing whitespace found out there). The fix rewrites the parser to take `value = last2` from apr_strtok's own save pointer and requires `name && *name && value && *value`, so a valueless cookie is skipped instead of synthesising a pointer past the end. Classed oob-read after the advisory's crash signature; note the NUL writes are a real out-of-bounds write too. fixed_in: CHANGES lists the CVE under 'Changes with Apache 2.4.9'; the 2.4.x backport 9e659703d4 is contained in the superseded 2.4.8 tag. Trunk commit is 0559370e7e2bf322d11d6df51b934d211fb2465c (same diff, same line numbers). VERDICT blind: the read and the NUL writes walk off a bump-allocated apr_pstrdup slice into whatever request object the pool allocated next in the same memnode -- no header, no size, no redzone, and nothing between the two objects to fault on.

trigger: Two or more Require directives naming the same LuaAuthzProvider with different arguments. All of them share one provider record, so an argument-less Require silently reuses the last-parsed argument array (the published access-control bypass). Because Require is OR_AUTHCFG, one of those lines can come from a .htaccess file, whose parse pool is the request pool -- the array then outlives its pool and a later request reading it dereferences recycled arena memory.
notes: Affects 2.3.x and 2.4.x through 2.4.10. Allocation sites read in 69eb3c6cfc^ (2.4.10): the provider record is a process-lifetime singleton, modules/lua/mod_lua.c:1806 'spec = apr_pcalloc(cmd->pool, sizeof(*spec));' (SIZE EXPRESSION sizeof(lua_authz_provider_spec) = 5 pointers, struct at :64-70), registered once per provider name into the global hash at :1811. Every Require line then overwrites that one object's args field: :1705 'spec->args = apr_array_make(cmd->pool, 2, sizeof(const char *));' (SIZE EXPRESSION apr_array_make nelts=2 x sizeof(const char*), grown by APR_ARRAY_PUSH at :1707), and only inside 'if (require_line && *require_line)' at :1703 -- so an argument-less Require leaves the previous line's pointer in place. :1711 '*parsed_require_line = spec;' hands the authz framework the shared singleton instead of a per-directive value; it is read back at :1747-:1759 (prov_spec->args->nelts, APR_ARRAY_IDX). MEMORY-SAFETY HALF, verified structurally by reading both ends, not reproduced: Require is registered AP_INIT_RAW_ARGS(..., OR_AUTHCFG) at modules/aaa/mod_authz_core.c:672 and its parse_require_line callback is invoked at :421 with cmd->pool, which for .htaccess is the request pool ('parms.pool = r->pool', server/config.c:2111) -- so an args array pushed into the pconf singleton from a .htaccess Require outlives its pool, and any later request whose Require has no arguments reads it. Within httpd.conf alone the same defect is pure aliasing with no lifetime violation, which is why the advisory frames it as an access-restriction bypass. Fix 69eb3c6cfc (2.4.x svn r1642861; trunk 38535f55b12814315ba5ded4a6180e11e821134e, svn r1642499) splits a per-Require lua_authz_provider_func {spec, args} out of the shared spec. VERDICT blind: apr_pool_clear rewinds active->first_avail without zeroing (apr_pools.c:968) and allocator_free pushes whole memnodes back onto allocator->free[index] (apr_pools.c:458,469) rather than calling free(), with max_free_index defaulting to APR_ALLOCATOR_MAX_FREE_UNLIMITED (apr_pools.c:182) so the munmap/free branch at :486-489 is disabled -- the stale apr_array_header_t stays mapped and readable, its nelts and element pointers are simply whatever the recycled memnode now holds, and there is no revocation, quarantine or scrub to notice.

trigger: POST to a Lua script that calls r:parsebody(), with Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=<B>, and a body crafted so that the next occurrence of <B> lies fewer than 8 bytes after the \r\n\r\n that ends a part's headers (the boundary itself is attacker-chosen and sscanf'd with %250c, so it may even contain CR/LF and match at the separator itself).
notes: Affects 2.4.51 and earlier. Allocation site read in 07b9768cef^ (2.4.51): modules/lua/lua_request.c:414 'buffer = (char *) apr_pcalloc(r->pool, vlen+1);'. SIZE EXPRESSION: vlen+1, where vlen is 'size_t vlen' set at :413 to 'end - crlf - 8'; 'end' is the next boundary found starting AT crlf (ap_lua_binstrstr at :409), so end-crlf can be 0..7 and vlen underflows. With end-crlf==7 vlen==SIZE_MAX and vlen+1==0: apr_palloc(pool,0) is a legal zero-byte bump (apr_pools.c:830 APR_ALIGN_DEFAULT(0)==0; the overflow guard 'if (size < in_size)' at :835 is not taken; :845-847 bump first_avail by 0) and returns the live cursor of the active memnode, after which :415 'memcpy(buffer, crlf + 4, vlen);' writes an unbounded length starting exactly at that cursor. Other underflow values (end-crlf 0..6) make vlen+1 huge, wrap APR_ALIGN_DEFAULT and hit the :835 guard, which calls httpd's abort_fn. Fix is one line, 'if (end - crlf <= 8) break;' -- trunk e1a199e8fd4d3a1c54b20446fd5a6de869d76e0b (svn r1895970), 2.4.x 07b9768cef (svn r1896039), whose commit subject says only 'mod_lua: Improve error handling'. VERDICT blind: apr_palloc has no per-object header, size record, redzone or free bit (apr_pools.c:846-847), there is no apr_pfree at all, and pool objects are adjacent inside the memnode -- so the memcpy walks over 'multipart' (apr_pcalloc(r->pool,256) at :383), 'key' and 'filename' (apr_pcalloc(r->pool,256) at :411,:412) and every later r->pool object with no bounds event of any kind. Secondary OOB READ in the same loop, not fixed by a contributor: :416 'sscanf(start + len + 2, ...)' is not bounded by the end of the pool body buffer.

affected_function: lua_read_body, consumed by req_parsebody (r:parsebody) and lua_ap_requestbody (r:requestbody)
trigger: Request to a Lua script calling r:parsebody() carrying 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=<B>' but no readable body, so ap_should_client_block(r) is false. lua_read_body then returns OK having written neither out-parameter, and the caller parses through an uninitialized pointer. Same reachable through r:requestbody() on a POST/PUT with no body.
notes: STACK, NOT HEAP -- recorded as system-malloc per the survey's convention for stack objects; the memory is neither an apr pool nor malloc. Affects 2.4.52 and earlier; CHANGES calls it 'Use of uninitialized value of in r:parsebody ... a read to a random memory area which could cause the process to crash'. Sites read in 1b96582269^ (2.4.52): lua_read_body is modules/lua/lua_request.c:233-268; its only writes to the out-parameters, ':252 *rbuf = (const char *) apr_pcalloc(r->pool, (apr_size_t) (length + 1));' and ':253 *size = length;', sit inside 'if (ap_should_client_block(r))' at :241, while :236/:267 return rc == OK when that branch is not taken. The objects the bug actually touches are therefore the CALLER'S UNINITIALIZED AUTOMATICS, with no allocation call at all: in req_parsebody 'apr_size_t size;' at :377 and 'const char *data;' at :390, passed by address at :394 and then dereferenced at :401 'start = strstr((char *) data, multipart);' -- a wild pointer read whose target is not statically determinable; 'size' is likewise used as the haystack length at :409 'ap_lua_binstrstr(crlf, (size - (crlf - data)), multipart, len)'. The same defect in lua_ap_requestbody is worse: 'apr_off_t size;' at :459 and 'const char *data;' at :468, then :473 'lua_pushlstring(L, data, (size_t) size);' copies an arbitrary length from an arbitrary address straight into a Lua string. SIZE EXPRESSION: none -- these are frame slots (8 bytes each); the pool allocation that should have produced them is 'apr_pcalloc(r->pool, (apr_size_t)(length + 1))' at :252, never reached on the bug path. Fix 1b96582269 (2.4.x svn r1898694) adds '*rbuf = NULL; *size = 0;' at the top of lua_read_body (and '*size = 0;' in lua_write_body) and returns DONE when the body cannot be read. VERDICT caught, reasoned explicitly: a stack canary does NOT catch this -- a canary guards writes past the frame, and this is a READ of an uninitialized automatic -- but the object is still reachable by instrumentation that an equivalent pool bug is not. MSan and valgrind track definedness of stack slots, and compiler init-on-entry hardening (-ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero/pattern) turns the wild pointer into a deterministic NULL/pattern deref at the point of use. The apr-pool counterpart has no such hook: apr_palloc hands back recycled bytes with no allocation event to instrument (apr_pools.c:846-847), apr_pool_clear rewinds first_avail without zeroing (:968) and there is no apr_pfree to mark anything undefined -- which is the contrast this row exists to record.

trigger: Over HTTPS, after a Lua script calls r:wsupgrade(), send a websocket data frame whose declared payload length (7-bit, 16-bit or 64-bit form) is larger than what one pass of the input filter chain delivers in the first bucket -- up to just under HUGE_STRING_LEN*1024 = 8388608. r:wsread() returns the declared length, and the bytes beyond what actually arrived are stale memory.
notes: Affects 2.4.53 and earlier. Defect read in 2.4.53 modules/lua/lua_request.c:2244 'memcpy(buffer, data, len);' -- it copies the REQUESTED len, not the 'data_length' that apr_bucket_read actually delivered at :2242, so it reads past the end of the delivered bytes. SOURCE of the over-read -- RE-CHECKED against the source, and it is pool memory, NOT bucket-allocator memory. Settled at two lines: modules/ssl/ssl_engine_io.c:1685 'apr_bucket_transient_create(start, len, f->c->bucket_alloc);' passes f->c->bucket_alloc only to allocate the apr_bucket STRUCT, while the data pointer is 'start', set at :1574 to 'inctx->buffer' and filled in place at :1642 'status = ssl_io_input_read(inctx, inctx->buffer, &len);'; and apr-util buckets/apr_buckets_simple.c:51-52, the read function that apr_bucket_type_transient installs at :133, is 'simple_bucket_read' -- '*str = (char *)b->data + b->start; *len = b->length;' -- it returns the caller's pointer verbatim with no copy into apr_bucket_alloc storage. So apr_bucket_read at lua_request.c:2242 hands mod_lua a pointer directly into the c->pool inctx buffer, and alloc_arena stays apr-pool. (Note ssl_engine_io.c:1575/:1639-1641 'apr_size_t len = sizeof(inctx->buffer); if (readbytes < len) len = (apr_size_t)readbytes;' caps one filter pass at 8192 bytes, which is why a frame declaring up to ~8MB over-reads by nearly the whole declared length.) The over-read object on the pre-fix code path: pre-fix lua_websocket_readbytes was only reached when 'plaintext == 0', i.e. TLS, so the first bucket is mod_ssl's transient bucket over its input context buffer -- allocation site read at modules/ssl/ssl_engine_io.c:2224 'inctx = apr_palloc(c->pool, sizeof(*inctx));' (SIZE EXPRESSION sizeof(bio_filter_in_ctx_t), which embeds 'char buffer[AP_IOBUFSIZE]' at :332, AP_IOBUFSIZE=8192 from include/httpd.h:311); the bucket is made at :1671/:1685 'apr_bucket_transient_create(start, len, f->c->bucket_alloc)'. DESTINATION read at modules/lua/lua_request.c:2388 'char *buffer = apr_palloc(r->pool, plen+1);' (SIZE EXPRESSION plen+1, plen attacker-declared and bounded only by 'plen < (HUGE_STRING_LEN*1024) && plen > 0' at :2384) -- apr_palloc, not pcalloc, so the tail is also stale arena bytes even without the memcpy. :2418 'lua_pushlstring(L, buffer, (size_t) plen);' hands the whole declared length to the Lua script. Fix 3a561759fc (2.4.x svn r1901503; trunk 11a3fcbf9e64239d8fe8402d941bbdcbc4532c88, svn r1901502) replaces the memcpy with apr_brigade_flatten plus 'if ((rv == APR_SUCCESS) && (delivered < len)) rv = APR_INCOMPLETE;' and makes every caller bail on non-success. VERDICT blind: the over-read leaves an 8192-byte array inside a c->pool object and continues into whatever the connection pool bump-allocated after it; apr pools keep no per-object size or redzone and apr_pool_clear rewinds first_avail without zeroing (apr_pools.c:968), so the disclosed bytes are stale decrypted plaintext from earlier reads on the same connection plus adjacent pool objects, with no bounds event. If the producer is instead the core input filter (plain HTTP, which only reaches readbytes in 2.4.54+ code), the source object is 'buf = apr_bucket_alloc(*len, a->list)' with *len = APR_BUCKET_BUFF_SIZE = 8000 at apr-util buckets/apr_buckets_socket.c:34 -- arena apr-bucket-alloc, equally header-less; apr-pool is recorded because that is the arena on the path the CVE actually reaches.

trigger: A configuration whose macro body contains a line at least MAX_STRING_LEN-1 (8191) characters long. process_content() copies each body line with strncpy(line, src, MAX_STRING_LEN - 1), which writes no NUL when the source is that long, leaving the 8192-byte buffer unterminated; substitute_macro_args() and the following apr_pstrdup() then scan past the end of the buffer.
notes: CONTROL-GROUP row. Affects through 2.4.57. Stack buffer, not heap: the object overread is 'char line[MAX_STRING_LEN];' at c41eb3b14a^:modules/core/mod_macro.c:457, a local array in process_content() -- MAX_STRING_LEN is HUGE_STRING_LEN = 8192 (include/httpd.h:305,308), so the size expression is a fixed 8192 bytes of stack frame, no allocator involved. Buggy copy read at mod_macro.c:468 ('strncpy(line, ((char **) contents->elts)[i], MAX_STRING_LEN - 1);'); the fix replaces it with apr_cpystrn(line, ..., MAX_STRING_LEN), which always terminates. The reads that run off the end are at :469 (substitute_macro_args -> next_substitution scans to '\0') and :479 ('*new = apr_pstrdup(pool, line);' -> strlen). The SOURCE string is pool memory -- 'apr_psprintf(pool, "%s" APR_EOL_STR, line)' at mod_macro.c:198, which is how a body line can reach 8192+ bytes after ap_cfg_getline read up to MAX_STRING_LEN-1 and the EOL was appended -- but the overread is of the stack destination, so alloc_arena is system-malloc per the stack-buffer rule. Verdict caught, with the caveat that a stack frame is itself a bump-allocated region: unlike an APR pool, stack objects are the one thing every deployed mitigation instruments (stack protector canary, ASan stack redzones, and a static frame layout the compiler knows), so this overread is detectable in a way an identical overread inside a pool memnode is not.

trigger: A backend script or proxied origin returns a Content-Type response header whose quoted media parameter ends in a single trailing backslash, e.g. 'text/plain; charset="x\'. analyze_ct() walks the quoted string; is_quoted_pair(cp) sees '\\' and reads *(cp+1), which is the NUL terminator. apr_isascii('\0') is true, so it reports a valid quoted pair and the caller does cp += 2, stepping the cursor one byte PAST the terminator; the loop condition then reads that byte.
notes: Affects 2.4.1 through 2.4.25 (also fixed on 2.2.x as 9016722b3e8d6eb0f85270c7f5ed21012cc2c9ea for 2.2.33/2.2.34). Buggy code read at d98d3a43^:modules/http/mod_mime.c:531-537 (is_quoted_pair, the useless '(s + 1) != NULL' test and the missing 'c &&' check) and :675-676 ('else if (is_quoted_pair(cp) > 0) { cp += 2; }' inside the quoted-parameter loop of analyze_ct). The object overread is the string passed as analyze_ct(r, r->content_type) at mod_mime.c:942. Allocation site read at d98d3a43^:server/util_script.c:634 -- 'tmp = apr_pstrdup(r->pool, l);' -- and ap_set_content_type() stores that pointer without copying (modules/http/http_protocol.c:1078-1083 at the same revision), so r->content_type IS the apr_pstrdup'd request-pool string; size expression is strlen(header value)+1. Verdict blind: apr_pstrdup is a bump allocation with no header and no trailing red zone, so the byte one past the NUL is simply the first byte of whatever object was bump-allocated next out of the same memnode -- a fully valid read with no bounds metadata to consult.

trigger: httpd configured as a forward proxy (ProxyRequests on) receiving a request-target whose scheme is 'unix' with a '|' but no ':' after it (e.g. "unix:|"): ap_proxy_de_socketfy() returns NULL and the caller immediately dereferences it.
notes: Affects 2.4.7 through 2.4.51; fixed in 2.4.52 (backport of trunk r1895914 + r1895921). Object: the proxy URL string. Allocation site read: `r->filename = apr_pstrcat(r->pool, "proxy:", r->uri, NULL);` at modules/proxy/mod_proxy.c:787 in the pre-fix revision (`git show a962ba7304^:modules/proxy/mod_proxy.c`), on r->pool, size 6 + strlen(r->uri) + 1; the handler passes *url = r->filename + 6. Path read: ap_proxy_pre_request() calls `*worker = ap_proxy_get_worker(r->pool, NULL, conf, *url);` -> ap_proxy_get_worker_ex(), which does `url = ap_proxy_de_socketfy(p, url);` and then `c = ap_strchr_c(url, ':');` at modules/proxy/proxy_util.c:1746. ap_proxy_de_socketfy (modules/proxy/mod_proxy.c) returns NULL when the 'unix:...|' form has no ':' in the tail, and ap_strchr_c is plain strchr (include/httpd.h:2345), so this is strchr(NULL, ':'). The fix adds `if (!url) { return NULL; }` immediately after the de_socketfy call, plus load-time checks in add_pass/add_member/set_proxy_param/proxysection. The second half of the CVE (SSRF to a declared UDS endpoint in mixed forward/reverse configs) is a routing-semantics issue with no memory violation and is not what this row records. Verdict reasoning as for CVE-2024-38477: the string that should have been there is pool memory, so the arena offers no detection; the fault itself is a zero-page trap. ARENA CAVEAT (added in merge for consistency across the null-deref rows): a NULL dereference faults on the unmapped zero page under ANY allocator, so this row is NOT evidence of arena blindness in the way the oob-read/oob-write and use-after-free rows are. alloc_arena/verdict here describe where the containing object lived, not a missed detection. || VERDICT NORMALISED BY THIS SESSION: counted 'caught' because a NULL dereference is trapped by page protection on any hardware, independent of the allocator. It is NOT evidence that the arena is visible to CHERI, and it is NOT evidence of blindness either; it is excluded from the blind count on purpose so the headline figure stays conservative. alloc_arena still records the true origin of the object.

trigger: A request whose proxied URL has no authority component (e.g. a mod_rewrite [P] or handler-forced proxy target such as "http:/path"), so apr_uri_parse() leaves uri->hostname NULL; with ProxyPreserveHost off, ap_proxy_create_hdrbrgd() then computes the Host header from uri->hostname.
notes: Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.59; fixed in 2.4.60 (backport of trunk r1918606, 'validate hostname'). Object: the apr_uri_t the proxy fills in. Allocation site read: `uri = apr_palloc(p, sizeof(*uri));` at modules/proxy/mod_proxy_http.c:1992 in the pre-fix revision (`git show 1d98d4db18^:modules/proxy/mod_proxy_http.c`); p is r->pool, allocation size is sizeof(apr_uri_t). Deref site: `if (ap_strchr_c(uri->hostname, ':'))` at modules/proxy/proxy_util.c:4499 (same pre-fix revision); the fix inserts `if (!uri->hostname) { rc = HTTP_BAD_REQUEST; goto cleanup; }` there and an equivalent guard in ap_proxy_determine_connection at proxy_util.c:3116. Checked explicitly that this is a genuine NULL and not an uninitialized-pool read: apr_palloc does NOT zero, but apr_uri_parse() memsets the whole struct at apr/uri/apr_uri.c:840, so hostname is a true NULL. Verdict reasoning: the struct carrying the NULL field is pool memory (bump-allocated, no header, no redzone, never freed individually), so an allocator-level checker sees nothing here -> blind per the arena rule. Borderline: a NULL dereference faults on the unmapped zero page, so this particular bug is caught by the MMU regardless of allocator; 'blind' records only that the arena contributes no detection. || VERDICT NORMALISED BY THIS SESSION: counted 'caught' because a NULL dereference is trapped by page protection on any hardware, independent of the allocator. It is NOT evidence that the arena is visible to CHERI, and it is NOT evidence of blindness either; it is excluded from the blind count on purpose so the headline figure stays conservative. alloc_arena still records the true origin of the object.

trigger: A malicious backend returns a Set-Cookie header containing MORE THAN ONE path= (or domain=) attribute, with ProxyPassReverseCookiePath / ProxyPassReverseCookieDomain configured.
notes: The size expression and the write offsets are computed from different iterations of the same loop -- a size/offset desynchronisation, which is the purest form of the intra-arena overflow this survey is about. Pre-fix modules/proxy/proxy_util.c allocates at :1080 `ret = apr_palloc(r->pool, len + pdiff + ddiff + 1);` (and :1106 `apr_palloc(r->pool, len + ddiff + 1)`), where pdiff/ddiff are the accumulated length DELTAS of every path=/domain= rewrite the loop matched. But poffs/doffs -- the offsets the writes are placed at, :1085-1096 -- are overwritten on each match and therefore describe only the LAST attribute. With two path= attributes in one Set-Cookie the two disagree, and the memcpy/strcpy run past the end of the allocation. Allocation size expression: apr_palloc(r->pool, len + pdiff + ddiff + 1). Verdict blind: the destination is a bare bump allocation out of r->pool with no header, no recorded length and no redzone, so the overflow lands in the neighbouring request object rather than in allocator metadata that a checker could validate. Fix resets `newpath = NULL; pdiff = 0;` (and the domain equivalents) whenever a subsequent attribute is found, so that only the last one is meaningful, per RFC 6265 5.3. Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.67.

trigger: A malicious or compromised AJP backend returns an AJP message whose declared body length is exactly max_size, so the 4-byte header plus body overruns the message buffer by 4 bytes.
notes: Off-by-header-length write of 4 attacker-controlled bytes past the end of a pool buffer. Pre-fix modules/proxy/ajp_msg.c:169 checked only `if (msglen > msg->max_size)`, but the caller writes the body AFTER the 4-byte header already in the buffer: modules/proxy/ajp_link.c:98 `ilink_read(sock, msg->buf + hlen, blen)` with hlen = msg->header_len = AJP_HEADER_LEN = 4. So an msglen of exactly max_size writes bytes [4, 4+max_size) into a buffer of max_size. Allocation site modules/proxy/ajp_msg.c:567 `msg->buf = (apr_byte_t *)apr_palloc(pool, size);` with size = AJP_MSG_BUFFER_SZ = 8192 (modules/proxy/ajp.h:135); the containing struct is apr_pcalloc'd at :563. Allocation size expression: apr_palloc(pool, 8192). Verdict blind: a bare bump allocation, so the 4 overflow bytes land in whatever pool object was allocated next in the same memnode; there is no allocator header to corrupt (which is what would normally be detected) and no redzone. Fix tightens the bound to `msglen > (msg->max_size - AJP_HEADER_LEN)`. Affects through 2.4.66.

trigger: A malicious AJP backend sends a truncated message so that a getter's last byte sits exactly at msg->len.
notes: Five sibling off-by-one bounds checks fixed in one commit -- a good example of the same defect replicated across an accessor family. Pre-fix modules/proxy/ajp_msg.c used `>` where `>=` was required: :398 `if ((msg->pos + 3) > msg->len)`, :423 `if ((msg->pos + 1) > msg->len)`, :446 same for peek_uint16, :467 `if (msg->pos > msg->len)` for peek_uint8, :485 same for get_uint8. Each admits a read of one byte at offset msg->len. Same allocation site as the sibling AJP issues: modules/proxy/ajp_msg.c:567 `msg->buf = (apr_byte_t *)apr_palloc(pool, size)`, size = AJP_MSG_BUFFER_SZ = 8192. Note msg->len is the message length, not the buffer length, so the read is in-buffer but out-of-message in the common case; it becomes a true out-of-allocation read when len reaches max_size, which the sibling CVE-2026-28780 shows is attainable. Verdict blind: no per-object bound exists to check against -- the pool records neither the size nor the extent of msg->buf. Affects through 2.4.66.

trigger: A malicious AJP backend sends a string field whose declared length runs to the end of the message with no NUL terminator, so the returned const char* is unterminated.
notes: Improper null termination promoted to an unbounded over-read. Pre-fix modules/proxy/ajp_msg.c:510 checked `(size + start > msg->max_size)` -- against max_size (the BUFFER size, 8192) rather than msg->len (the MESSAGE size), and with no check that the byte at buf[start+size] is actually NUL. The function then hands the caller a pointer into msg->buf that is treated as a C string, so every later strlen/strcpy/apr_pstrdup on it runs past the message and past the buffer until it happens to find a zero byte. Allocation site modules/proxy/ajp_msg.c:567 `msg->buf = (apr_byte_t *)apr_palloc(pool, size)`, size = AJP_MSG_BUFFER_SZ = 8192 (modules/proxy/ajp.h:135). Verdict blind: this is exactly the shape the pool cannot defend -- the scan leaves the 8192-byte object and continues through adjacent live pool objects in the same memnode with no boundary of any kind between them, so it terminates on unrelated request data rather than faulting, disclosing that data to the client. Fix changes the bound to `size + start >= msg->len` and adds an explicit `if (msg->buf[start + size] != '\0')` terminator check. Affects through 2.4.66.

trigger: A malicious AJP backend sends a data message shorter than the fixed header overhead, making the length subtraction wrap.
notes: Unsigned underflow that becomes a heap over-read and memory disclosure. Pre-fix modules/proxy/ajp_header.c:838 computes `expected_len = msg->len - (AJP_HEADER_LEN + AJP_HEADER_SZ_LEN + 1 + 1);` with no lower-bound check on msg->len. For a msg->len below that 7-byte overhead the subtraction wraps to a huge apr_size_t, which is then used as the chunk length handed back to the caller, so mod_proxy_ajp forwards far more of the buffer (and whatever follows it) to the client. Allocation site modules/proxy/ajp_msg.c:567 `msg->buf = (apr_byte_t *)apr_palloc(pool, size)`, size = AJP_MSG_BUFFER_SZ = 8192. Verdict blind: the wrapped length is never validated against any recorded extent because the pool records none; the read walks out of the 8192-byte object into adjacent live pool memory in the same memnode. Fix adds `if (msg->len < AJP_HEADER_LEN + AJP_HEADER_SZ_LEN + 1 + 1) return AJP_EBAD_HEADER;` before the subtraction. Affects through 2.4.66.

trigger: A malicious backend FTP server returning a malformed reply to EPSV (or PASV) that fails to tokenize, so the parse-failure branch closes a data socket that was never created.
notes: Affects 2.0.35-2.0.63 and 2.2.0-2.2.13; fixed in 2.2.14 (this commit is the 2.2.x backport of trunk r814652 + r814785). Allocation site read: `apr_socket_t *sock, *local_sock, *data_sock = NULL;` at modules/proxy/mod_proxy_ftp.c:779 in the pre-fix revision (`git show b10a9ef8b8^:modules/proxy/mod_proxy_ftp.c`) -- STACK LOCAL, NOT HEAP. data_sock is only created at :1238 (`apr_socket_create(&data_sock, ...)`) INSIDE the `if (pstr)` success branch; the failure branch at :1275-1277 does `apr_socket_close(data_sock)` with data_sock still NULL, and the PASV path repeats the shape at :1367-1369. The fix deletes both else-branches, replaces the strtok-based EPSV parsing with a validating parse_epsv_reply(), and guards the later close with `if (data_sock)` at :1853. Verdict reasoning: control-group row per the stack rule -- the NULL pointer lives in a stack slot, no arena involved, and the fault is a zero-page trap. Secondary finding, co-fixed by the same commit and NOT what the advisory scopes: the pre-fix EPSV parser reads out of bounds on pool memory at :1219 `*(pstr + strlen(pstr) + 1)` (one byte past the NUL of the strtok'd token, i.e. past the end of the allocation when the reply is a single token) and at :1232 `atoi(pstr + 3)` (unbounded when the token is shorter than 3). That string is ftpmessage, allocated `*pmessage = apr_pstrdup(r->pool, message);` at modules/proxy/mod_proxy_ftp.c:648, size strlen(message)+1 on r->pool -- an apr-pool object, and that read WOULD be blind. Both NVD (CWE-476) and the vendor advisory scope CVE-2009-3094 to the NULL dereference, so the row follows them rather than promoting the OOB read. ARENA CAVEAT (added in merge for consistency across the null-deref rows): a NULL dereference faults on the unmapped zero page under ANY allocator, so this row is NOT evidence of arena blindness in the way the oob-read/oob-write and use-after-free rows are. alloc_arena/verdict here describe where the containing object lived, not a missed detection.

trigger: A malicious backend FTP server that answers a control-channel command with a reply line shorter than four bytes (e.g. a bare LF), so fewer than four bytes of the response buffer are ever written.
notes: Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.41; fixed in 2.4.43 (backport of trunk r1873745, 'trap bad FTP responses'). Allocation site read: `char response[MAX_LINE_LEN];` at modules/proxy/mod_proxy_ftp.c:384 in the pre-fix revision (`git show 179492ff35^:modules/proxy/mod_proxy_ftp.c`), MAX_LINE_LEN is 80 -- STACK BUFFER, NOT HEAP, so it belongs to no APR pool and no malloc arena. ftp_string_read() initialises only response[0] (`buff[0] = 0;` at :231) and the NUL it writes at the copied length; on a short reply response[1..3] keep whatever the previous stack frame left. ftp_getrc_msg then reads them at :397-398 (`!apr_isdigit(response[1]) || !apr_isdigit(response[2]) || (response[3] != ' ' ...)`) and copies from `response + 4` into the caller's message buffer at :403, which becomes the proxy error text returned to the client -- an uninitialized stack disclosure. The fix threads an *outlen out of ftp_string_read and rejects nread < 4. Verdict reasoning: control-group row. The object never touches an apr_pool_t, so the arena question does not apply; recorded system-malloc + caught per the stack rule. Honest caveat: a heap allocator would not catch this either -- what catches it is MSan / -ftrivial-auto-var-init / stack poisoning, not the allocator. It is here as a control, not as a malloc win.

trigger: An untrusted backend returns HTML that mod_proxy_html rewrites, driving the buffer-growth path.
notes: CONTROL-GROUP ROW, and a valuable one because it sits inside httpd itself: mod_proxy_html is the rare in-tree module whose scratch buffer is NOT pool memory. Pre-fix modules/filters/mod_proxy_html.c:205 `newbuf = realloc(ctx->buf, ctx->avail);` -- plain libc realloc, with the growth loop at :202-203 `while (len > (ctx->avail - ctx->offset)) ctx->avail += ctx->cfg->bufsz;` and the unchecked copy at :219 `memcpy(ctx->buf+ctx->offset, buf, len);`. Only the enclosing saxctxt struct is pool memory (:857 `fctx = f->ctx = apr_pcalloc(f->r->pool, sizeof(saxctxt))`); the character buffer it points at is malloc-family. Allocation size expression: realloc(ctx->buf, avail) where avail grows in cfg->bufsz steps. Verdict caught: an overflow past a realloc'd chunk corrupts glibc chunk metadata and is detected by the allocator's own consistency checks, by ASan redzones, or by a hardened allocator -- none of which exist for the pool-backed siblings in this survey. Fix rewrites the module onto httpd's ap_varbuf API (ap_varbuf_grow / ap_varbuf_strmemcat / ap_varbuf_regsub), removing preserve() and pappend() entirely. Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.67.

trigger: A request carrying BOTH Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, proxied over a backend connection that has not yet been established (the common case: a freshly acquired, not-reused proxy_conn_rec).
notes: Affects 2.4.41 to 2.4.46; fixed in 2.4.48. Object: the proxy_conn_rec whose ->connection field is still NULL. Allocation site read: `conn = apr_pcalloc(ctx, sizeof(proxy_conn_rec));` at modules/proxy/proxy_util.c:1623 in the pre-fix revision (`git show fa22b50457^:modules/proxy/proxy_util.c`), inside connection_constructor(); ctx is a subpool created there with apr_pool_create(&ctx, pool) and tagged 'proxy_conn_pool', parented on the worker's reslist pool, so the object outlives any single request. Read site: `conn_rec *origin = p_conn->connection;` at modules/proxy/mod_proxy_http.c:579, dereferenced at `origin->keepalive = AP_CONN_CLOSE;` at modules/proxy/mod_proxy_http.c:639 (both pre-fix). Verified the ordering that makes origin NULL: proxy_http_handler calls ap_proxy_http_prefetch() at mod_proxy_http.c:2056, BEFORE ap_proxy_connect_backend()/ap_proxy_connection_create_ex() at :2088/:2098 set backend->connection; the pcalloc leaves ->connection NULL until then. The fix is the 2.4.x backport of trunk r1678771 ('The proxy connection may be NULL during prefetch, don't try to dereference it'), whose trunk commit is 8c162db8b65b2193e622b780e8c6516d4265f68b (2015, verified: not an ancestor of 2.4.46, is an ancestor of 2.4.48); it only reached 2.4.x bundled inside the upgrade/tunneling backport fa22b50457, which deletes exactly that line. Verdict reasoning as for CVE-2024-38477. ARENA CAVEAT (added in merge for consistency across the null-deref rows): a NULL dereference faults on the unmapped zero page under ANY allocator, so this row is NOT evidence of arena blindness in the way the oob-read/oob-write and use-after-free rows are. alloc_arena/verdict here describe where the containing object lived, not a missed detection. || VERDICT NORMALISED BY THIS SESSION: counted 'caught' because a NULL dereference is trapped by page protection on any hardware, independent of the allocator. It is NOT evidence that the arena is visible to CHERI, and it is NOT evidence of blindness either; it is excluded from the blind count on purpose so the headline figure stays conservative. alloc_arena still records the true origin of the object.

trigger: A crafted request uri-path routed to a uwsgi:// backend where strlen(worker->s->name) is larger than the URL that follows the 'proxy:' prefix in r->filename -- notably when the generic 'proxy:reverse' worker is selected (RewriteRule [P] to a uwsgi:// target), so the worker name bears no relation to r->filename.
notes: Affects 2.4.30 through 2.4.48; fixed in 2.4.49 (backport of trunk r1892805). Object: r->filename. Allocation site read: `found = apr_pstrcat(r->pool, "proxy:", real, use_uri + len, NULL);` at modules/proxy/mod_proxy.c:950 in the pre-fix revision (`git show 6d9672bf09^:modules/proxy/mod_proxy.c`), assigned `r->filename = found;` at :971; size = 6 + strlen(real) + strlen(use_uri + len) + 1, on r->pool. (The forward-proxy variant is apr_pstrcat(r->pool, "proxy:", r->uri, NULL) at :787/:797.) Out-of-bounds sites, modules/proxy/mod_proxy_uwsgi.c in the same pre-fix revision: :477 `w_len = strlen(worker->s->name);`, :481 `u_path_info = r->filename + 6 + w_len;`, :482 `if (u_path_info[0] != '/')` -- a read past the end of the pstrcat'd string; then :485 `ap_unescape_url(url + w_len - delta)`, which scans from the out-of-bounds pointer until it happens to find a NUL and can write a '\0' back into whatever it decodes; then :491 `apr_table_add(r->subprocess_env, "PATH_INFO", url + w_len - delta)`, which copies those out-of-bounds bytes into a CGI variable handed to the backend. Fix replaces all of it with `u_path_info = ap_strchr(url + sizeof(UWSGI_SCHEME) + 2, '/')`. Blind: apr_palloc is a bare bump pointer (apr_pools.c:846-847) with no per-object header, no size, no redzone and no free bit, so reading past the end of r->filename lands inside the next live object in the same memnode -- nothing faults, and the bytes disclosed into PATH_INFO are other pool objects of the same request/connection.

trigger: A trusted proxy (RemoteIPProxyProtocol enabled for it) sends a crafted PROXY protocol header. v2 path: the 16-bit length field is unchecked, so ctx->need becomes up to 16+65535 and the read loop memcpy's that much into ctx->header, which is only sizeof(proxy_header) bytes. v1 path: the underlying filter can return more than was asked for in AP_MODE_GETLINE, so hdr->v1.line can be longer than 108 bytes before the CR is found, and strcpy() then overruns a 108-byte stack buffer.
notes: Affects 2.4.33 through 2.4.39; verified fixed_in with 'git tag --contains e3f30ad646' -> first release tag 2.4.41 (the Apache 2.4 page's version list is easy to misread here). TWO buffers, and the survey-relevant one is NOT the stack one. (1) POOL buffer: 'char header[sizeof(proxy_header)]' is a member of remoteip_filter_context (mod_remoteip.c:130-138 at e3f30ad646^), and the allocation site read at mod_remoteip.c:1068 is 'ctx = f->ctx = apr_palloc(f->c->pool, sizeof(*ctx));' -- size expression sizeof(remoteip_filter_context), of which the header field is sizeof(proxy_header) = max(sizeof(proxy_v1)=108, sizeof(proxy_v2)=12+1+1+2+216=232) = 232 bytes, out of the CONNECTION pool. The overflowing write is 'memcpy(ctx->header + ctx->rcvd, ptr, len);' at :1111, driven by 'ctx->need = MIN_V2_HDR_LEN + remoteip_get_v2_len(...)' at :1140-1141 with no upper bound; the fix adds exactly 'if (ctx->need > sizeof(proxy_v2))'. (2) STACK buffer: 'char buf[sizeof(hdr->v1.line)]' at :775 with 'strcpy(buf, hdr->v1.line);' at :798 -- 108 bytes, stack, not heap; this is the half the advisory names 'stack buffer overflow'. Verdict blind is for the pool half: ctx is bump-allocated from c->pool with no header, no size and no red zone, so writing up to ~65 KB past a 232-byte field silently overwrites whatever the connection pool bump-allocated next (the ctx->bb brigade, the SSL filter contexts, request structures) with no bounds event and no scrub. The stack half would be caught by a stack canary or ASan redzone, which is precisely the asymmetry this survey is measuring. Advisory also notes a NULL pointer dereference: the pre-fix 'case 0x00: LOCAL' and unsupported-family arms at :989-997 return HDR_DONE leaving conn_conf->client_addr NULL.

trigger: A response body filtered by an OutputSed/InputSed substitution script, where a single logical line grows past the current line buffer. The s/// command path (command() SCOM -> dosub() -> copy_to_linebuf()) reallocates eval->linebuf while step_vars->loc1/loc2/locs still point into the previous buffer; subsequent substitution writes then land relative to a buffer that is no longer the live one. The pre-fix 'unsigned int reqsize' arithmetic in appendmem_to_linebuf can also wrap for large lengths so grow_line_buffer is skipped entirely.
notes: Affects 2.4.52 and earlier. Allocation site read at 943f57b336^:modules/filters/sed1.c:110 -- 'newbuffer = apr_pcalloc(pool, newsize);' inside grow_buffer(); size expression is newsize after 'if (newsize < *cursize * 2) newsize = *cursize * 2;' then '(newsize + ((1<<12)-1)) & ~((1<<12)-1)' (round up to 4 KB). The initial buffers come from sed1.c:269/273/277 -- 'eval->linebuf = apr_pcalloc(eval->pool, eval->lsize)' with eval->lsize = INIT_BUF_SIZE = 1024 (sed1.c:89). eval->pool is r->pool: mod_sed.c:247-248 passes r->pool to sed_init_eval(), which stores it as eval->pool (sed1.c:247). Verdict blind: grow_buffer never frees or scrubs the old buffer -- there is no apr_pfree -- so the abandoned linebuf stays live, readable and writable pool bytes, and the stale step_vars->loc1/loc2 pointers into it produce neither a bounds event nor a use-after-free event. A write that runs off the end of the new apr_pcalloc'd buffer simply lands in the next object bump-allocated from the same memnode. The complete fix is two commits: 943f57b336 (apr_size_t arithmetic + step_vars resync after a linebuf move) and e266bd09c313a668d7cca17a8b096d189148be49 (mod_sed.c sed_write_output flow fix so the output buffer is not used after clear_ctxpool).

trigger: A Cookie header whose session value contains an '&'-delimited pair made up entirely of '=' characters, e.g. a pair of exactly '='. apr_strtok(pair, "=", &plast) skips the separators, finds an empty remainder and returns NULL at apr_strtok.c:38-39 WITHOUT ever assigning *last, so plast stays NULL; the immediately following apr_strtok(NULL, psep, &plast) then does 'str = *last;' (NULL) and dereferences it in 'while (*str && strchr(sep, *str))'.
notes: Borderline call, reasoning stated. Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.46; same fix commit as CVE-2021-26691 (it merges two trunk revisions). Buggy sequence read at 97c9e9d66c^:modules/session/mod_session.c:405-408 ('char *plast = NULL; ... char *key = apr_strtok(pair, psep, &plast); char *val = apr_strtok(NULL, psep, &plast);'); the fix moves the val call inside 'if (key && *key)'. The early-return-without-setting-*last is at apr/strings/apr_strtok.c:38-39 and the fatal load at apr_strtok.c:31-35. The string being tokenized is pool memory -- allocation site read at mod_session.c:402, 'encoded = apr_pstrdup(r->pool, z->encoded);', size strlen(z->encoded)+1 out of r->pool -- but the pointer actually dereferenced is the uninitialised-to-NULL stack local plast, not that buffer. Verdict caught: a load through NULL traps at the unmapped zero page independently of the allocator, so this row does not exhibit arena blindness; it is recorded because the surrounding parse operates entirely on pool strings. VERDICT NORMALISED IN MERGE: this row was submitted as `caught`, reasoned (correctly) from the fault being taken on the zero page. It is recorded as `blind` so that the verdict column stays a mechanical function of alloc_arena across the whole survey; the detection here comes from the MMU, not from the allocator, exactly as the caveat above says. || VERDICT NORMALISED BY THIS SESSION: counted 'caught' because a NULL dereference is trapped by page protection on any hardware, independent of the allocator. It is NOT evidence that the arena is visible to CHERI, and it is NOT evidence of blindness either; it is excluded from the blind count on purpose so the headline figure stays conservative. alloc_arena still records the true origin of the object.

trigger: An origin server (or any handler mod_session is proxying/serving for) sets a SessionHeader-driven session with more than one key/value entry. identity_count() sizes the encode buffer at strlen(key)*3 + strlen(val)*3 + 1 per entry, which pays for the '=' but not for the '&' that identity_concat() writes between entries, so the buffer is short by exactly (number of entries - 1) bytes.
notes: Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.46. Allocation site read at 97c9e9d66c^:modules/session/mod_session.c:365 -- 'buffer = apr_pcalloc(r->pool, length + 1);' -- where length is accumulated by apr_table_do(identity_count, &length, z->entries, NULL) at :364. The undercount is the '+ 1' at mod_session.c:321 ('*count += strlen(key) * 3 + strlen(val) * 3 + 1;'), which the fix changes to '+ 2'. The overrunning writes are in identity_concat at :331 ('*slider = '&'; slider++;') and :336-338 ('*slider = '='; slider++; ap_escape_urlencoded_buffer(slider, val);') -- one byte of overflow per entry after the first, attacker-influenced in count and, through the final ap_escape_urlencoded_buffer, in content. Size expression: sum over entries of 3*strlen(key) + 3*strlen(val) + 1, plus 1. Pool is r->pool. Verdict blind: apr_pcalloc is the same bump pointer as apr_palloc with a memset (apr_pools.c:846-847), there is no header, no size and no guard byte after the request-pool object, so the extra bytes land in whichever object was bump-allocated next from the same memnode and no bounds check exists to fire.

trigger: Plain HTTP spoken to an HTTPS port while a third-party module has taken over ap_hook_process_connection(), so the handshake failure (MODSSL_ERROR_HTTP_ON_HTTPS) surfaces from ssl_io_filter_output() rather than ssl_io_filter_input(). ssl_io_filter_output() passes its own ap_filter_t* to ssl_io_filter_error(), which hands it to ssl_io_filter_disable(), which does 'bio_filter_in_ctx_t *inctx = f->ctx;' -- but the OUTPUT filter's ctx is an ssl_filter_ctx_t, not a bio_filter_in_ctx_t.
notes: Affects 2.4.1 through 2.4.25. Miscast read at a0403e8220^:modules/ssl/ssl_engine_io.c:941 ('bio_filter_in_ctx_t *inctx = f->ctx;') reached from :1755 ('return ssl_io_filter_error(f, bb, status, 0);' inside ssl_io_filter_output, whose own line 1729 is 'ssl_filter_ctx_t *filter_ctx = f->ctx;'). Allocation site read at ssl_engine_io.c:2052 -- 'filter_ctx = apr_palloc(c->pool, sizeof(ssl_filter_ctx_t));' -- ssl_filter_ctx_t is 6 pointers (ssl_engine_io.c:105-112), i.e. 56 bytes on LP64. The type it is reinterpreted as, bio_filter_in_ctx_t (ssl_engine_io.c:308-320), is over 8 KB because of its 'char buffer[AP_IOBUFSIZE]' member, and its final member 'ssl_filter_ctx_t *filter_ctx' sits at roughly offset 8264. So line 945 'inctx->filter_ctx->pssl = NULL;' reads a pointer ~8.2 KB beyond a 56-byte allocation and then writes NULL through it. Its sibling allocation, the real inctx, is 'apr_palloc(c->pool, sizeof(*inctx))' at ssl_engine_io.c:2022. Verdict blind: both objects are bump-allocated from the same connection pool with no type tag, no size record and no bounds; the 8 KB overread stays inside c->pool's memnodes and reads whatever a later apr_palloc handed out, so nothing distinguishes the confused pointer from a legitimate one. Advisory calls it a NULL pointer dereference; the source shows a type confusion whose crash is an out-of-bounds pointer load followed by a store through it.

trigger: An attacker-controlled OCSP responder (or a proxy in front of it) accepts only part of each write, so apr_socket_send returns a short count.
notes: CONTROL-GROUP ROW, stack storage rather than either heap arena. Pre-fix modules/ssl/ssl_util_ocsp.c:136 advances the cursor by the wrong variable: `wbuf += remain;` where it must be `wbuf += wlen;`. On a short send (wlen < remain) the pointer jumps the FULL remaining length while the counter only drops by what was actually sent, so the loop condition `remain > 0` keeps it going and the next apr_socket_send transmits from beyond the end of the buffer -- disclosing adjacent stack contents to the OCSP responder. Buffer is stack, not heap: modules/ssl/ssl_util_ocsp.c:75 `char buf[HUGE_STRING_LEN];` inside send_request, filled by :128 `BIO_read(request, buf, sizeof buf)`. alloc_arena is recorded as system-malloc because none of the three httpd arenas apply; 'stack buffer, not heap' is the accurate description. Verdict caught is the borderline call in this survey and is qualified: a stack CANARY would not fire, because this is a read and it is past the buffer rather than over the return address. But ASan's stack redzones and any stack-bounds-checking scheme do catch it, and unlike the pool rows the object here has a compiler-known extent that a checker can be derived from -- which is the property the arena rows lack. Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.67.

trigger: On a threaded MPM (worker/event) with a reachable /server-status handler: request server-status repeatedly while other worker threads are concurrently updating their scoreboard slots. mod_status reads worker_score->client/request/vhost straight out of shared memory with no snapshot, so it can observe a moment where the fixed-size char array has been partially rewritten and carries no NUL.
poc: https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/34133
notes: Affects httpd before 2.4.10 (also 2.2.x before 2.2.29). Pre-fix revision read is b2605d20c4^. ALLOCATION SITE: the object over-read is a worker_score, which lives in the scoreboard shared mapping -- server/scoreboard.c:137-139 `scoreboard_size = sizeof(global_score); scoreboard_size += sizeof(process_score)*server_limit; scoreboard_size += sizeof(worker_score)*server_limit*thread_limit;` and scoreboard.c:184 `rv = apr_shm_create(&ap_scoreboard_shm, scoreboard_size, fname, pool);` (scoreboard.c:230 for the anonymous variant, scoreboard.c:330 `ap_calloc(1, scoreboard_size)` when built SB_NOT_SHARED). ap_init_scoreboard carves it with raw pointer arithmetic, scoreboard.c:154-165: `more_storage = shared_score; ... ap_scoreboard_image->servers[i] = (worker_score *)more_storage; more_storage += thread_limit * sizeof(worker_score);` -- no per-slot header, no redzone, slots directly adjacent. The over-read fields are fixed arrays inside that struct: include/scoreboard.h:115-117 `char client[40]; char request[64]; char vhost[32];`. WRITER: server/scoreboard.c:487-491 the serving worker updates them in place with apr_cpystrn(ws->client,...) / copy_request(ws->request, sizeof(ws->request), r) / apr_snprintf(ws->vhost,...) while a request is in flight. READER: modules/generators/mod_status.c:309 and :640 `ws_record = ap_get_scoreboard_worker_from_indexes(i, j);` hands out a raw pointer INTO the shm, and mod_status.c:750-756 (and :835-841 for the short report) then passes those raw pointers to ap_escape_html(r->pool, ws_record->request) etc. If the racing writer has overwritten the terminator, ap_escape_html walks off the 64-byte field, through the adjacent worker_score slots, and off the end of the mapping -- the classic heap over-read, and the escaped copy it builds in r->pool then reflects other workers' request lines (credential disclosure). mod_status also allocates its own two pool buffers on the same request pool, mod_status.c:237-238 `pid_buffer = apr_palloc(r->pool, server_limit * sizeof(pid_t)); stat_buffer = apr_palloc(r->pool, server_limit * thread_limit * sizeof(char));` -- those are correctly sized and are NOT the overflowed object; they are noted only because they are the 'status buffer' the advisory language can be read as pointing at. VERDICT blind: the shm arena is a single flat mapping with no per-slot bounds, so nothing distinguishes reading slot i's request[] from reading slot i+1's -- and for the last slot the walk simply runs off the mapping. The fix adds ap_copy_scoreboard_worker (server/scoreboard.c, new function in this commit) which memcpy's the whole worker_score into a caller-owned buffer -- mod_status.c now uses `worker_score *ws_record = apr_palloc(r->pool, sizeof *ws_record);` -- and force-terminates client/request/vhost. Note the fix converts a shm over-read into a copy into an apr-pool object: correct, but the pool copy is itself unguarded, so the safety comes entirely from the explicit NUL writes.

trigger: Untrusted markup passed through mod_xml2enc (typically behind mod_proxy_html) where the configured skipto pattern matches, so the buffer pointer is advanced.
notes: A two-field length invariant broken on one path. In fix_skipto (modules/filters/mod_xml2enc.c) the pre-fix code advances the buffer start pointer `ctx->buf = p;` (:167) and decrements only the byte counter `ctx->bytes -= (p-ctx->buf);` (:166), leaving ctx->bblen -- the recorded buffer LENGTH -- unchanged. Downstream code derives sizes from the pair, e.g. :516 and :519 use `ctx->bblen - ctx->bytes`, so after the skip the computed span overstates the bytes actually remaining between ctx->buf and the end of the allocation by exactly (p - old buf). Allocation site modules/filters/mod_xml2enc.c:384 `ctx->buf = apr_palloc(f->r->pool, (apr_size_t)(ctx->bblen+1));` (and the initial :132 `ctx->buf = apr_palloc(r->pool, (apr_size_t)ctx->bblen)` with ctx->bblen = BUFLEN at :131). Allocation size expression: apr_palloc(r->pool, bblen+1). Verdict blind: bblen IS the only record of the object's size -- the pool keeps none -- so once bblen and the real extent disagree there is nothing left that could notice, and the overflow runs into the adjacent bump-allocated object. Fix adds the missing `ctx->bblen -= (p-ctx->buf);`. Affects 2.4.0 through 2.4.67.

trigger: ASAN verdict 'Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1'. The harness passed a second 76-byte fuzzer string as the DESTINATION buffer (the current harness instead does `new_dst = malloc(new_str_len*3+1);` at fuzz_utils.c:93 before the call at :94): `char *ns10 = af_gb_get_null_terminated(&data2, &size2); ... ap_escape_path_segment_buffer(ns10, ns11);` (the harness as it stood before oss-fuzz b9369041cc05). ap_escape_path_segment_buffer emits up to 3 bytes per input char plus a NUL (c2x at server/util.c:2030-2040), so up to 226 bytes went into a 76-byte allocation.
poc: not public; OSS-Fuzz testcase behind authentication
fix_commit: oss-fuzz b9369041cc05 (projects/apache-httpd/fuzz_utils.c) - the harness now does malloc(strlen(ns11)*3+1)
notes: CONTROL-GROUP row, and it is a HARNESS bug, not an httpd bug - I read the fix diff and it changes only the fuzzer. Recorded because the contrast is the survey's whole argument: the identical write in production httpd goes into `server/util.c:2080 return ap_escape_path_segment_buffer(apr_palloc(p, 3 * len + 1), segment);`, a bump-carved pool object with no bounds, and would be seen by nothing. The one publicly readable 'WRITE' finding in this project exists only because the harness used malloc. The OSV record's git range is junk (repo AFLplusplus, introduced == fixed); do not treat that hash as a fix.

affected_function: ap_is_chunked (httpd server/util.c:1788, with static find_last_token at :1760 inlined)
trigger: ASAN verdict 'Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1', crash state ap_is_chunked / fuzz_utils.c. Reached by `ap_is_chunked(pool, new_str)` at projects/apache-httpd/fuzz_utils.c:148, added to the harness in oss-fuzz 4978312d616e (2021-11-15); the first crash was filed four weeks later.

fixed_in: unknown - OSV names e2d995aa7220d4ec0b416d9fb63500253e2305c8, which in the httpd clone is 'Add a Travis build job ... OpenSSL 3', a bisection endpoint and not a semantic fix
notes: MECHANISM UNRESOLVED, stated rather than guessed. `line` is a 76-byte malloc from `ada_fuzz_header.h:39 char *new_s = malloc(STR_SIZE + 1);`, which is why ASAN saw it; that is the arena determination and it is solid. The obvious candidate is `*s` after `while (--s > line)` (server/util.c:1803-1808) when find_last_token returns `line` itself, which leaves s at line-1 - but I brute-forced 6.0 million inputs over an alphabet of the relevant characters against a verbatim transcription of the current source and could NOT reach it, because the preceding exact-match `ap_cstr_casecmp(line, "chunked")` appears to make lidx==0 unreachable. Positive control in the same run confirms the loop does leave s<line when s starts at line, so the search was capable of firing. In production the argument is apr_table_get(r->headers_in,"Transfer-Encoding"), an r->pool string (server/protocol.c:348), where a one-byte under-read is invisible.

trigger: ASAN verdict 'Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1', crash state identical to OSV-2021-1679 (ap_is_chunked / fuzz_utils.c). Filed separately three weeks later, so the earlier report had not actually been fixed.
poc: not public; OSS-Fuzz testcase behind authentication
fixed_in: unknown - OSV names ed611d3754bc38f2d9c9aabf0fb7becd8d8fdc7d, which in the httpd clone is 'Revert r1896758 and r1896746 (travis debug temporaries)', a bisection endpoint and not a semantic fix
notes: Duplicate signature of OSV-2021-1679; kept as its own row because it is a separate public issue with its own record and shows the first one was never resolved. Same allocation site (`ada_fuzz_header.h:39 malloc(STR_SIZE + 1)`), same unresolved mechanism - see the OSV-2021-1679 notes for the brute-force result and its positive control.

trigger: Encoder-stream instructions that keep inserting entries with empty names and values until the first eviction. An entry is appended before older entries are evicted, so the count momentarily exceeds capacity/32 by one and dt->elts[dt->nelts++] writes one slot past the array.
notes: ALLOC SITE READ: src/http/v3/ngx_http_v3_table.c, ngx_http_v3_set_capacity(): pre-fix `elts = ngx_alloc(max * sizeof(void *), c->log);`, post-fix `ngx_alloc((max + 1) * sizeof(void *), c->log)`, with max = capacity / 32. CLEANEST CONTROL-GROUP ROW IN THE SURVEY: the QPACK dynamic table deliberately does NOT use the pool -- it uses ngx_alloc/ngx_free directly (ngx_free(dt->elts) and ngx_free(dt->elts[n]) are visible in the same file), so the entry array is an ordinary malloc block with exact bounds and an exact free. A one-pointer overwrite past its end is precisely what a CHERI-bounded pointer traps on, and unlike every ngx-pool row here there is no adjacency to silently corrupt. Introduced by 987bee4363d1 per the commit message. Advisory title 'Buffer overwrite in HTTP/3'; mapped to this commit by the CVE text 'undisclosed HTTP/3 ENCODER INSTRUCTIONS'. Vulnerable 1.25.0-1.25.5, 1.26.0.

trigger: A crafted QUIC session that closes the QPACK encoder stream and opens another one. The session-level dynamic table keeps dt->insert_buffer, which was allocated from the encoder stream's own pool.
poc: HTTP/3 session that opens an encoder stream, causes a dynamic-table insertion, closes the encoder stream, then opens a new one
notes: ALLOC SITE READ: src/http/v3/ngx_http_v3_table.c:171 `dt->insert_buffer = ngx_create_temp_buf(c->pool, h3scf->max_table_capacity);` -- the fix changes c->pool to c->quic->parent->pool. ngx_create_temp_buf (src/core/ngx_buf.c:12-44) makes TWO allocations: the ngx_buf_t header via ngx_calloc_buf(pool) (~120 bytes, a bump allocation) and the data via ngx_palloc(pool, size) at ngx_buf.c:22. The stale pointer dt->insert_buffer is a pointer to the ngx_buf_t, so the first faulting access is on the pool-resident header. Second-order detail worth recording: the QUIC stream pool is ngx_create_pool(NGX_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE=16384) at src/event/quic/ngx_event_quic_streams.c:693, giving pool->max = 4095, and max_table_capacity is hardcoded to 4096, so the DATA block is one byte over the threshold and is therefore a `large` allocation = a real malloc that ngx_destroy_pool does ngx_free (ngx_palloc.c:80-85). So a revoking allocator would see the data block die but not the ngx_buf_t's own object boundary, and any pointer into the 16 KB stream-pool block is equally stale. Introduced by d7dd7e9ae4c2110f753cac02fd702eefef9fce16 (1.31.0, 'HTTP/3: optimize encoder stream memory usage'), which is exactly why the advisory range is only 1.31.0-1.31.1. Companion hardening: 9e293766e73c469c015df5341f1c1d403fb532c6 (avoid recreation of standard client uni streams) and 875750a4f76bf68189929f887951e02b66c99801. Advisory severity: major. || Object: dt->insert_buffer = ngx_create_temp_buf(pool, h3scf->max_table_capacity) at src/http/v3/ngx_http_v3_table.c:171-172. max_table_capacity is the hardcoded NGX_HTTP_V3_MAX_TABLE_CAPACITY = 4096 (src/http/v3/ngx_http_v3.h:46), which is ONE byte above pool->max = 4095, so the data area takes ngx_palloc_large -> real malloc (ngx_palloc.c:220) and is genuinely ngx_free()d when the encoder stream's pool is destroyed (ngx_palloc.c:89-95). That makes the payload half a real caught case -- a hardened/quarantining allocator sees the free and the reuse. Caveat recorded honestly: the accompanying ngx_buf_t header (ngx_calloc_buf -> ngx_pcalloc(pool, sizeof(ngx_buf_t)), 80 bytes measured, ngx_buf.c:17) IS a bump carve and is only freed at block granularity, so the header half is blind. Verdict caught on the strength of the 4096-byte payload. The one-byte-over-4095 accident is the whole reason this row differs from its neighbours. Fix moves the allocation to c->quic->parent->pool. Advisory text confirmed in the fetched CHANGES under 1.31.2.

trigger: An HTTP/3 request timed to land during connection draining. Creating a decoder stream inside ngx_http_v3_send_cancel_stream() calls ngx_get_connection(), which calls ngx_drain_connections(), which drains the SAME request stream again -- unbounded recursion until the stack is exhausted, or, if stream creation fails first, the request-stream connection is drained while still referenced further up the stack.
notes: ALLOC SITE READ: the used-after-free object is an ngx_connection_t taken from the worker-wide recycling free list -- src/core/ngx_connection.c:1229 `c = ngx_cycle->free_connections;` and returned at :1279-1280 `c->data = ngx_cycle->free_connections; ngx_cycle->free_connections = c;`. The backing store is one array allocated ONCE per worker at src/event/ngx_event.c:754-755 `cycle->connections = ngx_alloc(sizeof(ngx_connection_t) * cycle->connection_n, cycle->log);`. CLASSIFIED ngx-pool/blind DELIBERATELY, and this is the judgement call worth reviewing: the array is literally malloc'd, but ngx_free is NEVER called per connection, so no allocator event ever marks the object dead, no revocation sweep ever fires, and a stale ngx_connection_t pointer stays a valid in-bounds capability that is then handed to the NEXT client. That is arena behaviour built on top of malloc, and calling it 'system-malloc/caught' on the strength of the ngx_alloc call would invert the finding. The per-stream pool is ngx_create_pool(NGX_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE) at src/event/quic/ngx_event_quic_streams.c:693 and IS ngx_free'd on destroy, so the pool half of the object would be caught. Advisory title 'Stack overflow and use-after-free in HTTP/3'; the commit message documents both halves explicitly, and the CVE text ('specifically timed during the connection draining process') matches the ngx_drain_connections recursion exactly. Vulnerable 1.25.0-1.25.5, 1.26.0.

trigger: An HTTP/3 request containing a zero-length literal field line. st->literal.length == 0 took the done path without ever assigning st->value.data, so header handlers received an ngx_str_t with a NULL data pointer.
notes: The fix adds `st->value.data = (u_char *) "";` at three sites in src/http/v3/ngx_http_v3_parse.c (in field_lri, field_l and field_lpbi). ALLOC SITE READ for the non-degenerate path: src/http/v3/ngx_http_v3_parse.c:649 `st->last = ngx_pnalloc(c->pool, n + 1);` (and :1151/:1162 ngx_pnalloc(c->pool, name->len + 1) / (value->len + 1) in the header handler) -- i.e. when the length is non-zero the value IS a connection-pool bump allocation. VERDICT REASONING, again not following the arena rule: with length zero nothing is allocated at all, and the fault is a NULL dereference, which traps on CHERI and on a conventional MMU alike. Recorded as caught for that reason. Advisory title 'NULL pointer dereference in HTTP/3'; mapping from CVE text 'undisclosed HTTP/3 requests cause worker processes to terminate' plus the commit message 'st->value was passed with NULL data pointer to header handlers'. Vulnerable 1.25.0-1.25.5, 1.26.0.

trigger: Any path that reuses an ngx_quic_buffer_t after ngx_quic_free_buffer(). qb->chain was cleared but qb->last_chain was left pointing at chain links and buffers that had already been returned to the connection free lists.
notes: No CVE assigned -- the commit calls it 'use-after-free protection' for a potential rather than demonstrated bug, and it shipped in the same release as the four HTTP/3 CVEs. ALLOC SITE READ: the dangling references are to ngx_buf_t / ngx_chain_t from src/event/quic/ngx_event_quic_frames.c:56 `b = ngx_palloc(c->pool, sizeof(ngx_buf_t));` with data at :67 `p = ngx_pnalloc(c->pool, NGX_QUIC_BUFFER_SIZE);` (4096, defined at :13), and chain links from ngx_alloc_chain_link(c->pool) at :172. Blind for the same reason as CVE-2024-34161: ngx_quic_free_buf() does not free, it pushes onto qc->free_bufs and ngx_quic_alloc_buf() pops the buffer straight back with its contents intact, so no allocator event ever marks the object dead. The one-line fix is `qb->last_chain = NULL;` beside the existing `qb->chain = NULL;`.

trigger: Handshake-level CRYPTO frames sent AFTER the client's Finished message, in the same UDP packet as the Finished frame (which is why the CVE text requires an MTU of 4096 or more). The handshake send context and its crypto buffer chain have already been discarded, so the frame is written into and read back out of buffers that were returned to the connection's free list.
notes: ALLOC SITE READ: src/event/quic/ngx_event_quic_frames.c, ngx_quic_alloc_buf(): the ngx_buf_t at :56 `b = ngx_palloc(c->pool, sizeof(ngx_buf_t));` and the data at :67 `p = ngx_pnalloc(c->pool, NGX_QUIC_BUFFER_SIZE);` with NGX_QUIC_BUFFER_SIZE = 4096 (:13). THE DECISIVE DETAIL IS THE FREE PATH: ngx_quic_free_buf() does not free anything -- it pushes the buffer onto qc->free_bufs (`shadow->shadow = qc->free_bufs; qc->free_bufs = shadow;`) and ngx_quic_alloc_buf() pops it straight back off at the top of the same function, WITHOUT clearing the data. So a discarded handshake buffer is handed to the next consumer with its old contents intact, which is exactly the 'memory disclosure' the commit message describes. Classified ngx-pool/blind even though the 4096-byte data block is technically over the 4016 request-pool threshold, because the per-connection free list means ngx_free is never reached for the life of the connection and no revocation can fire. pool->max = min(pool_size - sizeof(ngx_pool_t), ngx_pagesize-1) at ngx_palloc.c:33-34; sizeof(ngx_pool_t)=80 on LP64, so the REQUEST pool (request_pool_size default 4096, ngx_http_request.c:584) bumps anything <= 4016 and mallocs above that, and the CONNECTION pool (connection_pool_size default 64*sizeof(void*)=512, ngx_event_accept.c:159) bumps only <= 432. CVE text: 'leak previously freed memory' on MTU >= 4096. Related hardening in the same release: 9ddc6a08f4c83db5acc0a74c223ddf75a44b726d (reset qb->last_chain in ngx_quic_free_buffer). Vulnerable 1.25.0-1.25.5, 1.26.0.

trigger: A QUIC packet with a flipped key phase bit sent before the next-generation keys exist. The code selected &pkt->keys->next_key.client unconditionally and passed its NULL cipher context to the decryption routine.
notes: The fix guards on `pkt->keys->next_key.client.ctx != NULL` in src/event/quic/ngx_event_quic_protection.c, falling back to trial decryption with the current keys (RFC 9001 section 6.3) so that the timing side channel is also closed. ALLOC SITE READ for the containing object: src/event/quic/ngx_event_quic.c:244 `qc->keys = ngx_pcalloc(c->pool, sizeof(ngx_quic_keys_t));` (the connection itself at :239 `qc = ngx_pcalloc(c->pool, sizeof(ngx_quic_connection_t));`) -- connection-pool allocations, and because ngx_pcalloc zeroes, the unpopulated next_key.ctx is reliably NULL rather than garbage. VERDICT REASONING: a NULL dereference traps regardless of arena, so caught. Note that had this field been ngx_palloc'd instead of ngx_pcalloc'd, the same bug would have been an uninitialized-pointer dereference into stale pool bytes -- a genuinely blind bug -- which is a useful illustration of how much the pcalloc/palloc choice carries here. Mapping to this commit is inferred from the advisory title ('NULL pointer dereference in HTTP/3', vulnerable 1.25.3 only) plus the commit's stated 'fixes segfault while accessing missing next keys'; the nginx-announce for 1.25.4 names the CVE pair but not the commits.

trigger: A QUIC session where ngx_quic_shutdown_stream() fails inside the stream connection's cleanup handler. sc->connection kept pointing at a connection the application code had already freed, so a second close was attempted on it.
notes: The fix resets sc->connection to NULL on the error path. ALLOC SITE READ: the doubly-closed object is a QUIC stream ngx_connection_t plus its pool -- the connection comes off the recycling free list (src/core/ngx_connection.c:1229/:1279-1280, backing array ngx_alloc'd once at src/event/ngx_event.c:754-755) and the pool from src/event/quic/ngx_event_quic_streams.c:693 `pool = ngx_create_pool(NGX_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE, c->log);`. TWO HALVES, DIFFERENT ANSWERS: the pool half really is a double free at the system allocator (ngx_destroy_pool -> ngx_free on the block chain, ngx_palloc.c:89-95) and the commit message says exactly that -- 'allocator double free error' -- so that half would be caught; the ngx_connection_t half is never freed at all, only pushed back on ngx_cycle->free_connections, so the stale sc->connection stays a valid in-bounds capability that now belongs to a different client. Recorded blind for the connection half, which is the one the survey is about. Advisory title says 'Use-after-free in HTTP/3'; bug_class recorded as double-free because that is the mechanism the fix describes. Mapping inferred from the advisory range (1.25.0-1.25.3) and the commit message; the 1.25.4 announce names the pair without commits.

trigger: Binary upgrade of a worker inheriting an IPv6 listening socket. The text buffer was sized for NGX_INET6_ADDRSTRLEN + sizeof(":65535") - 1, but the formatted form is bracketed ([addr]:port), so two bytes more are written than were allocated.
notes: No CVE assigned, and not remotely triggerable -- it fires on binary upgrade with an IPv6 listen socket, so it is included as a clean, unambiguous small-object pool overflow rather than as a security finding. ALLOC SITE READ: src/core/ngx_connection.c:204 `ls[i].addr_text.data = ngx_pnalloc(cycle->pool, len);` with len set two lines up in the AF_INET6 case. The cycle pool is NGX_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE = 16384 so pool->max = 4095 and a ~54-byte address string is a bump allocation; the two bytes land on whatever the cycle pool handed out next. pool->max = min(pool_size - sizeof(ngx_pool_t), ngx_pagesize-1) at ngx_palloc.c:33-34; sizeof(ngx_pool_t)=80 on LP64, so the REQUEST pool (request_pool_size default 4096, ngx_http_request.c:584) bumps anything <= 4016 and mallocs above that, and the CONNECTION pool (connection_pool_size default 64*sizeof(void*)=512, ngx_event_accept.c:159) bumps only <= 432. The fix changes sizeof(":65535") to sizeof("[]:65535").

component: nginx/core / ngx_files (request body to temp file)
trigger: Writing a chunked-encoded client request body to a temporary file, when the special last buffer (cl->buf->pos == NULL) happens to be the only buffer left after a do/while iteration in ngx_write_chain_to_file(). Made easier to hit by 3832b608dc8d (1.9.13), which lowered the buffer count from IOV_MAX (~1024) to NGX_IOVS_PREALLOCATE (~64).
notes: The fix adds `if (ngx_buf_special(cl->buf)) continue;` to ngx_chain_to_iovec() at src/os/unix/ngx_files.c:359-363. ALLOC SITE READ for the containing objects: the request body buffers and their chain links come from r->pool (ngx_http_request_body.c allocates rb via ngx_pcalloc(r->pool, sizeof(ngx_http_request_body_t)) and the buffers via ngx_create_temp_buf on r->pool). VERDICT REASONING, not following the arena rule: the fault is reading through cl->buf->pos == NULL, i.e. a NULL dereference, which traps on CHERI and on a conventional MMU alike.
